title: Fix the capability-pinning wait, and the two gates that hide it
description:
Three separate measured defects in dependency order, written 2026-10-03 at
merged `714cc0c` (PR #8), tree clean.

Source plan: `~/.opencode/plan/house-fix.md`

| # | Defect | Blast radius | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `house_pipe_wait` spins in `wfe` inside an `unsafe` FFI call and pins its capability | `blk init` / `virtio init` hang; any colocation with a must-progress thread | diagnosed, not fixed |
| B | `scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp` requires a QEMU machine property absent on Ubuntu 24.04's `qemu-system-arm` | every virtio gate fails on CI in 14 ms | diagnosed, not fixed |
| C | `nightly.yml` is one sequential job; the first red gate aborts all later steps | most of the gate suite has never executed in CI | diagnosed, not fixed |

Defect A blocks Phase 4 steps 9-11. B and C are why it was never caught in CI.

A and B are independent and can be fixed in either order. C is a workflow-shape
change and should land last, once there is a green suite to split.

Plan section 8 states the intended split: one `bug` for A1, one for A2, one
`chore` for the gate work in sections 2-3, and one for the related latent defect
in section 1.6.
## Success criteria

- [ ] `house-irq-dispatch-check` new; red before the fix, green after
- [ ] `house-virtio-blk-check` green, and no longer passing vacuously (drive attached, non-zero capacity asserted)
- [ ] `house-virtio-transport-check` green (shares `virtioInit`)
- [ ] `house-driver-check`, `house-ipc-check` green
- [ ] `house-fork-check`, `house-preempt-check` green (the `parkLoop` `c_pipeWait` site)
- [ ] `house-spin-hotplug-check`, `smp-check`, `SMP_N=4 smp-check` green
- [ ] `house-yield-spin-check` green, and re-checked that it is green for the intended reason
- [ ] `rust-check` + `rust/c-abi.md` audit green
- [ ] `haskell-check` 327 host checks, 0 fail
- [ ] Per-change gate `make check` (hvf + tcg) green

Not run and therefore not claimed: `smp-check-8` (4 GiB), `vm-check`,
`house-dynamic-root-check` (QEMU 11+, local only).

## After this epic

Phase 4 steps 9-11 unblock once defect A is green. `docs/TOOLCHAIN.md` currently
claims virtio-blk reaches the device through an endpoint; that stays false until
Phase 4 step 10 lands.

title: house_pipe_wait pins its capability: spin in wfe inside unsafe FFI
description:
Defect A1. Diagnosed in full, not fixed.

## The mechanism

`c_pipeWait` is `foreign import ccall unsafe "house_pipe_wait"`
(`kernel/H/Interrupts.hs:64`, used at `kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs:106`).
Its body (`rust/crates/house-libc/src/threads/threads.rs:1771`) is a `wfe` spin
bounded only by `house_uptime_ns()`. No foreign-call boundary, no Haskell safe
point, for up to 5 ms per call — and the dispatcher calls it in a loop,
forever. GHC cannot preempt inside an `unsafe` foreign call, so the capability
is pinned for the whole wait. `forkIO` puts the child on the parent's local run
queue, so dispatcher and shell land on the same capability; the shell then never
gets scheduled again and never prints `ok capacity=`.

## The asymmetry that is the whole bug

`poll` (`threads.rs:1683`) already has the guard `house_pipe_wait` lacks
(`threads.rs:1712-1720`, inside `poll()`):

```rust
let has_runnable = { lock; !RUN_HEAD[core].is_null(); unlock };
if has_runnable {
    house_sched_yield();      // give the runnable thread the capability
} else {
    /* wfe spin loop with deadline */
}
```

`poll` and `house_pipe_wait` have opposite caller populations, and only the
former has the guard. `poll`'s only caller is the EL0 syscall path
(`rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/svc.rs:143`) — house-libc pthreads the house
scheduler owns outright, so `RUN_HEAD[core]` is authoritative for them.
`house_pipe_wait` has **no Haskell caller of `poll` anywhere in the tree** and
is instead called from GHC RTS threads, which reach it through a different
path. Those callers get no release point at all.

That also explains the two sites that work today: `parkLoop`
(`Process.hs:1310`) calls the same `c_pipeWait` and `house-fork-check` /
`house-preempt-check` pass, because the parked thread's supervisor is not
colocated with it on a capability. The dispatcher wedges because it is forked
*by the shell thread it then starves*.

## Premise to verify as part of the fix

The guard only helps if GHC's capability threads are house-libc `HouseThread`s,
so a runnable shell thread on the same capability appears in `RUN_HEAD[core]`.
GHC's threaded RTS creates its capabilities through the platform's
`pthread_create`, and house-libc implements that, so this is plausible — but it
is a premise, not a fact, and it is the difference between the fix working and
not. **Measure it.**

If the new gate goes green 10/10 the premise held and the diagnosis is confirmed
end to end. If it stays red, the premise is false — stop, and take a fallback.
Do not iterate on variations of this guard without re-checking the premise first;
if the shell's threads are not in `RUN_HEAD`, no amount of tweaking that flag
helps.

## Fix

In `rust/crates/house-libc/src/threads/threads.rs`, give `house_pipe_wait` the
same `has_runnable` -> `house_sched_yield()` pre-check `poll` has at line 1712.
Smallest change that matches existing style in the same file.

`house_sched_yield` (`threads.rs:565`) masks interrupts, spins on the scheduler
lock, reschedules the current *HouseThread*, and returns.

## Second at-risk call site, fixed by the same change

`Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs:1310`:

```haskell
_ <- liftIO (c_parkPipeFd >>= \fd -> c_pipeWait fd 5000)
```

Same function, same import, same defect, currently latent only because of where
the thread sits. Fixing `house_pipe_wait` in Rust fixes both. Fixing it in
Haskell per-import would not guarantee anyone remembers the second site.

## Fallback, if the premise fails

In order of preference:

- **6a.** Have `house_pipe_wait` park through the house-libc scheduler
  (`house_sched_block`, which already does `wfe` and re-checks the run queue)
  instead of its own spin loop.
- **6b.** Make `house_pipe_wait` return a bounded slice and let the *Haskell*
  caller loop, so the spin never spans more than one scheduler slice. This
  reintroduces polling and needs the poll budget measured, not guessed.
- **6c.** Fix the fork placement: start the dispatcher at boot rather than
  lazily inside `installHandler`, so it never shares a capability with a
  command handler. This treats the symptom and should be the last resort.

Whichever is chosen, record in the commit message why the `poll`-guard shape was
insufficient.

## Regression net

Confirm still green: `house-fork-check`, `house-preempt-check`,
`house-spin-hotplug-check`, `smp-check`, `smp-check-8`. `parkLoop`'s
`c_pipeWait` is covered by `house-fork-check`; if it is not, say so rather than
assuming.

Not run and therefore not claimed: `smp-check-8` (4 GiB, expensive),
`vm-check`, `house-dynamic-root-check` (needs QEMU 11+, local only).

`rust-check` plus a `rust/c-abi.md` audit: `threads.rs` changes, but
`house_pipe_wait`'s signature is unchanged, so the exported-symbol map must
still match.
## Steps to Reproduce

Every row is a full `make -C platform/aarch64 clean && make -C kernel clean && make house-build`, then QEMU under hvf with `-M virt,virtio-mmio-transports=8,gic-version=3` and a real `-drive` attached so the gate is not vacuous.

The isolation driver matches each command's **output** pattern (`ok device_id`, `ok capacity`), never the prompt, because the line editor redraws the prompt during echo and a prompt match reports 0 ms for everything.

| # | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | merged `714cc0c`, unmodified | **HANG** |
| B0 | `installHandler` does not fork the dispatcher | OK 23 ms |
| C0 | fork a thread whose body is only `C.yield` — no FFI, no locks | **HANG** |
| D0 | real `dispatcherLoop` + `C.yield` on **both** branches | **HANG** |
| E0 | fork a heartbeat thread: `c_uart_puts` then `C.yield` | OK 240 ms |
| F0 | real `dispatcherLoop`, `c_pipeWait` -> `C.yield` | **OK** |

Rates at A0: `virtio init 7` HANG 8/8. `blk init 7` HANG 8/10 — the two passes are the runs where the dispatcher fork won the race, not a second bug. `blk status 7` (171 ms) and `virtio scan` (190 ms) always pass, so the fault is in transport init, not `blkProbeCapacity`.

`blk init`'s own `serveEndpoint` fork was ruled out: stubbing it out changed nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `house-irq-dispatch-check` is **red** on the current tree (three iterations, not one)
- [ ] `house_pipe_wait` carries the same `has_runnable` -> `house_sched_yield()` pre-check `poll` has at `threads.rs:1712`
- [ ] Premise verified as part of the fix: gate green 10/10 confirms it; still-red means the premise is false and the fallback applies
- [ ] `house-virtio-blk-check`, `house-virtio-transport-check`, `house-driver-check`, `house-ipc-check` green
- [ ] `house-fork-check`, `house-preempt-check`, `house-spin-hotplug-check`, `smp-check`, `SMP_N=4 smp-check` still green (the `parkLoop` second call site)
- [ ] `rust-check` + `rust/c-abi.md` audit: exported-symbol map still matches (`house_pipe_wait`'s signature is unchanged)
- [ ] `haskell-check` 327 host checks, 0 fail
- [ ] Not claimed unless run: `smp-check-8` (4 GiB), `vm-check`, `house-dynamic-root-check` (QEMU 11+, local only)
close_reason: Fixed in 7e8ec98: the IRQ dispatcher's wait branch uses threadDelay 20000 instead of the blocking c_pipeWait FFI spin. The bead's poll-guard shape was rejected on evidence (RUN_HEAD holds house-libc pthreads; GHC green threads never enter it, so at -N1 there is nothing to yield to). Gate green 3/3 then 10/10; bounding the slice instead measured red 3/3. The two parkLoop c_pipeWait sites stay latent.

title: Add house-irq-dispatch-check gate (red before the fix, green after)
description:
Step 2 of the plan, and it must land **before** the fix so the fix has something
to turn green.

A dedicated gate, not `house-virtio-blk-check`: `virtio init 7` is 8/8 on the
buggy tree, so three consecutive successes is a reliable red.

## What to build

- `scripts/qemu-irq-dispatch-check.exp` — boot, run `virtio init 7` three times,
  assert an `ok device_id` within the bound each time, then assert the shell
  still answers `virtio status` afterwards (so a wedged-but-quiet machine cannot
  pass by timing out identically).
- `Makefile`: add `house-irq-dispatch-check` next to `house-virtio-blk-check`
  (line 239), add it to the `check` aggregate (line 495ff) and to `check-tcg`
  (line 473ff).

`scripts/gate-coverage.sh` fails if a new gate is not wired into `check` /
`check-tcg` / `nightly.yml`, so wire all of them in the same commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
 red on the current tree

Expect `virtio init` to hang on the first iteration.

## Why three iterations

`blk init` was 8/10, not 10/10. Any single-shot gate built on it is unreliable —
hence three iterations.

## Harness traps to not repeat

Two Expect harness bugs cost real time here:

1. In Tcl, `-re {"> "}` searches for the literal `"> "` because braces suppress
   substitution, so it matches nothing and every command looks like a hang.
2. A corrected `-re "> "` still matches the line editor's prompt redraw during
   echo, reporting 0 ms for everything.

Match each command's **output** pattern instead (`ok device_id`, `ok capacity`) —
the echo can never contain it.

title: Characterise A2: does Control.Concurrent.yield return the capability?
description:
Step 1 of the plan. **Do not skip this step.**

A2 is a defect *distinct* from A1 and is currently unexplained. It must be
characterised before it is fixed, because its blast radius is wider than the
dispatcher: the merged YIELD backoff in `Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs` and
anything else relying on `yield` to hand over the capability are equally suspect.

## What was measured

| # | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | fork a thread whose body is only `C.yield` — no FFI, no locks | **HANG** |
| E0 | fork a heartbeat thread: `c_uart_puts` then `C.yield` | OK 240 ms |
| F0 | real `dispatcherLoop`, `c_pipeWait` -> `C.yield` | **OK** |

C0 and E0 together say the dispatcher's *work* is irrelevant. A thread that does
nothing but `yield` still wedges; the same loop with one `c_uart_puts` added
does not. That falsified the working hypothesis at the time — "a missing
`C.yield`".

**A2 — `Control.Concurrent.yield` is not returning the capability.**
`H/Concurrency.hs:62` is `yield = liftIO IO.yield`, i.e. stock
`Control.Concurrent.yield`. If that actually yielded, C0 could not wedge.

Note the trap: adding `C.yield` around the `c_pipeWait` call is **not** a fix —
D0 proved that, and it is obvious in hindsight: the spin is *inside* the FFI
call.

## The characterisation

One build, three shell-visible counts, printed by a temporary `virtio`-less
shell path or read via `dmesg`:

1. a thread that loops `C.yield` forever, counting iterations;
2. a thread that loops `c_uart_puts` + `C.yield`, counting iterations;
3. a thread that loops `threadDelay 1` forever, counting iterations.

**If (1) counts far fewer iterations than (3) while both threads stay alive,
`yield` is not returning the capability and A2 is confirmed as a distinct
defect.**

**If (1) matches (3)**, C0 wedged for a different reason and this step has told
us nothing — in that case go straight to fixing A1 and treat A2 as open.

Cheaper alternative if the shell plumbing is awkward: `strings` the image for the
count format strings and read the counters off the UART trace. Same information,
no new command surface.

## Why this must precede the fix

The A2 fix differs depending on the answer, and guessing produces a fix that
passes the dispatcher gate and leaves the underlying scheduler bug live.

## If A2 cannot be answered cheaply

Fix A1 (which is fully diagnosed and sufficient to unblock) and file A2
separately rather than blocking on it.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Three counters exist and are readable (shell-visible output, or read off the UART trace via `strings` on the image for the count format strings)
- [ ] The `C.yield` count vs the `threadDelay 1` count is recorded as a measured number, not a description
- [ ] The verdict is recorded explicitly: either "A2 confirmed as a distinct defect" or "C0 wedged for another reason; A2 stays open"
- [ ] If confirmed, `house-yield-spin-check` is re-baselined before the A2 fix, so the fix has a before/after
close_reason: A2 confirmed as a distinct defect: bare yield starves timer-blocked threads at -N1 (a=14M hvf/22M tcg, c=0, main never woke); numbers in comments

comments.text:
# house-1hc.3 verdict: A2 CONFIRMED as a distinct defect

`Control.Concurrent.yield` (`H/Concurrency.hs:62`, `yield = liftIO IO.yield`)
does not return the single `-N1` capability to timer-blocked threads.

## Method (TEMP probe, fully reverted — final tree has zero kernel diff)

One-file TEMP probe in `kernel/Kernel/Shell/Loop.hs` only (every line
`TEMP-A2`, `git diff --stat` showed Loop.hs only, built under `-Wall -Werror`):
new `yieldcount` shell verb forks three Haskell threads each bumping its own
`IORef`, main sleeps 5 s + 200 ms two-sample check and prints
`yieldcount a=<n> b=<n> c=<n> alive=...`, then kills the threads:

- (a) tight `yield` loop (= `H.Concurrency.yield` body; `H` is a newtype over
  `IO`, `liftIO` is the constructor, so `Control.Concurrent.yield` in the
  `IO` shell is the identical operation)
- (b) `withCString "y" c_uart_puts` + `yield` loop (E0 shape)
- (c) `threadDelay 1` loop

Deviation from the plan's letter, same intent: because the wedge starves the
measuring main thread itself, each spinner also self-reports
`yieldlive <arm>=<count>` every 2M (a) / 200k (b) / 100k (c) iterations, so
numbers exist even when the final print never comes. (a)'s report duty is
1 UART puts per 2M yields (negligible; still essentially pure). Driven from
Expect with a hard timeout + `kill -9`, `-smp 1`, matching the `yieldlive` /
`yieldcount` patterns themselves, never the bare prompt. QEMU 11.1.2.

## hvf `-smp 1` (verbatim)

- `yieldlive a`: 7 lines, 2000001 ... last `a=14000007`
- `yieldlive b`: 74 lines (early ones are UART-interleave fragments of
  concurrent (a)/(b) prints, e.g. `b=20000`; clean tail +200k each), last
  `b=14200071`
- `yieldlive c`: **0 lines** — (c) never reached its first 100k report
- final `yieldcount a=...`: **0 lines** — main's 5 s `threadDelay` never
  completed inside the 40 s window
- `supervised thread died`: 0; shell handler errors: 0
- harness exit 2 (no prompt return; QEMU killed): machine wedged until killed

## tcg `-smp 1` (verbatim, same direction)

- `yieldlive a`: 11 lines, last `a=22000011`
- `yieldlive b`: 118 lines, last `b=23000115`
- `yieldlive c`: **0 lines**
- final `yieldcount a=...`: **0 lines** in the 120 s window
- deaths 0; harness exit 2 (wedged until killed)

## Verdict

**A2 confirmed as a distinct defect.** Bare-`yield` spinners (a) ran to
14M (hvf) / 22M (tcg) iterations while the `threadDelay`-blocked arm (c)
and the shell main thread (5 s sleep) were starved to zero for the whole
run — no crash, no error, pure scheduler starvation. Sign note for
`house-1hc.4`: the plan expected `(a) << (c)`; what was measured is
`(c) ~= 0 << (a)`, i.e. the timer arm is the starved party, not the yield
arm. Same conclusion (yield does not hand over the capability at `-N1`),
opposite sign. Both (a) and (b) progressed together, so `yield` does switch
among *runnable* threads; what never runs is anything woken by the timer —
consistent with the in-tree `parkLoop` comment (`Process.hs`: "`yield`
alone does not release the capability") and `4d4666e` ("bare yield never
freed it"), now reproduced at Haskell level with numbers.

## `house-yield-spin-check` re-baseline (before/after for house-1hc.4)

- With TEMP probe in tree: hvf `shell answered in 11ms`, tcg `16ms` (bound 60ms)
- Clean tree after revert: hvf `shell answered in 12ms`, tcg `27ms` (bound 60ms)
- EL0 `svc #0` spinner (parkLoop bounded backoff, `threadDelay 100` past 64
  spins) does NOT starve the shell — the EL0 layer has its release point;
  raw Haskell `yield` does not. Gate green for the intended reason.

## Revert verified

`grep -c TEMP-A2 kernel/Kernel/Shell/Loop.hs` -> 0, `git status --short`
clean, `make house-build` green, `make haskell-check` green (pure tests
PASS), `make house-yield-spin-check` green hvf+tcg on the clean tree.
No fix shipped here: `H/Concurrency.hs`, `Process.hs`, Rust, harnesses
untouched in the final diff.

title: Fix A2: yield does not return the capability
description:
Step 4 of the plan. **Only do this if the characterisation step confirmed
A2.**

## Fix, ranked by preference

- **4a.** Replace `H.Concurrency.yield`'s body with an explicit release point
  that is known to work in this RTS, and re-run the whole suite — A2's blast
  radius is every `yield` in the kernel.
- **4b.** If `yield` is fine and C0 wedged for a rate reason, drop this step and
  record that.

## The prohibition

**Do not paper over A2 by inserting an FFI call into hot loops to create
boundaries.** That is what made E0 pass; it converts a scheduler bug into a
per-site landmine.

## Blast radius to re-verify

A2's blast radius is every `yield` in the kernel. The merged YIELD backoff in
`Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs` (bounded-backoff arm past a threshold of 64
consecutive resumes) is equally suspect.

`house-yield-spin-check` must stay green, and must be re-checked that it is
green **for the intended reason** — that gate runs at `-smp 1` deliberately,
because at `-smp 2` both the fixed and unfixed arms are fast and the difference
is unobservable.

## Related evidence already in the tree

`docs/design/park-resume-capability-pinning.md` states that parking must
*return* from the unsafe `house_enter_el0` FFI so the RTS capability is released
while blocked. A bare `yield` was already measured insufficient (`4d4666e`:
"bare yield never freed it") — under the single-capability RTS a thread that is
immediately runnable again re-acquires the capability before a timer fires.
That is direct evidence that at least one `yield` site does not release.
## Steps to Reproduce

Inherit the C0/E0 measurement from the characterisation issue: fork a thread whose
body is only `C.yield` — no FFI, no locks — and observe the machine wedge, while
the same loop with one `c_uart_puts` added completes in ~240 ms.

Note that adding `C.yield` around the `c_pipeWait` call is **not** a fix — D0
proved that, and it is obvious in hindsight: the spin is *inside* the FFI call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `H/Concurrency.hs:62` is either replaced with an explicit release point known to work in this RTS, or the issue is closed with 4b recorded
- [ ] The full suite is re-run — A2's blast radius is every `yield` in the kernel
- [ ] `house-yield-spin-check` stays green **and** is re-checked as green for the intended reason (the gate runs at `-smp 1` deliberately)
- [ ] No FFI call was inserted into a hot loop to manufacture a boundary
close_reason: Landed as 9bb0285: H.yield is a 1us timer park; yield-spin-check green hvf+tcg

title: Virtio harness: probe for virtio-mmio-transports and stop passing vacuously
description:
Defect B, section 2 of the plan. Independent of defect A — fix in either order.

## Symptom

Nightly run `37136946248`, `slow-gates` job: fails in 14 ms with
`Property 'virt-8.2-machine.virtio-mmio-transports' not found` ->
`FAIL: eof before welcome`. Ubuntu 24.04 ships `qemu-system-arm` 8.2;
`virtio-mmio-transports` needs QEMU 10+.

This is the same QEMU-version requirement as `house-dynamic-root-check`, which
is already excluded from `check-tcg` **with a printed reason**.
`house-virtio-blk-check` was wired into nightly without the equivalent handling.

## Fix

- In `scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp`, probe for the property before building the
  `-M` argument string; fall back to plain `-M virt,gic-version=3` and print a
  single explicit line saying which property was dropped and why.
- Fall back to the 8-transport-less machine **and attach the device the old
  way**, so the gate stays non-vacuous. A skip that silently exercises nothing
  is worse than a failure.
- Add a `SKIP`-style banner the harness can grep, so the nightly log
  distinguishes "skipped, QEMU 8.2" from "passed".

## Second, independent problem in the same harness

With no `-device virtio-blk-device,drive=...` attached, every assertion takes
the `INFO` path and the gate **passes vacuously**. Add an explicit assertion
that the drive was attached and that the capacity probe returned a non-zero
sector count, so a misconfigured runner cannot report green.

The measurement harness used for section 1 attached a real 64 MiB image for
exactly this reason.

**Trap:** `house-virtio-blk-check` only fails when a drive is attached. Run
without `-device virtio-blk-device` it takes every `INFO` path and **passes** —
so a green run of `house-virtio-blk-check` proves nothing about the device
path. Any future "it's flaky, retry" instinct here is wrong; the pass is
vacuous.
close_reason: Guest widened to 32 virtio slots; all four virtio harnesses drop virtio-mmio-transports= and discover the device slot, so they run on QEMU 8.2 through 11+; qemu-virtio-blk.exp gained the missing non-vacuity guard. Also fixed two load-bearing 8-slot bounds the site enumeration missed: irq.rs house_irq_push ack range 48..56 -> 48..80 (slot>=8 livelocked in an IRQ storm) and Shell/Loop.hs handleConMirror's literal installConMirror 7 -> findConSlot. Verified hvf+tcg for driver/transport/net/con/irq-dispatch and hvf for blk; the blk tcg leg still hits a PRE-EXISTING slot-independent TCG livelock reproduced on pristine HEAD.

title: Split nightly.yml so one red gate does not abort the whole suite
description:
Defect C, section 3 of the plan. A workflow-shape change. **Should land
last**, once there is a green suite to split.

## Symptom

`nightly.yml` is a single job with sequential steps (`Filesystem and driver
gates`, `EL0 execution gates`, `SMP gates`, `Scaling gate`, `Memory matrix`,
`Miri`, `Slow SMP legs`). The first failure stops everything after it.

## Observed consequence

In run `37136946248` the virtio-blk failure meant these **never executed**:
`house-virtio-net-check`, `house-virtio-con-check`, the EL0 execution group,
the SMP group, `smp-check-8`, `vm-check`, `miri`, and the slow SMP legs.
`house-fs-check`, `house-ipc-check`, `house-driver-check` and
`house-virtio-transport-check` passed before it.

This is the root cause of the silence around defect A: **the gate that would
catch it has never been run.** Of the affected list, 5 were verified locally
during Phase 4 (`house-fs-check`, `house-ipc-check`, `house-driver-check`,
`house-virtio-transport-check`, `house-preempt-check`); the rest are unverified
anywhere. PR #8's green `gate` runs do not speak to it — `check.yml` runs
`make check-tcg`, which covers the Makefile's `check-tcg` legs only.

## Fix

Split into independent jobs on a matrix, or keep one job and give each gate group
`continue-on-error: true` plus a final `gate summary` step with `if: always()`
that fails the job if any group failed.

**The matrix is better**: it also parallelises, and each leg's result is visible
on its own.

## Also fix the schedule while here

`nightly.yml` was added 2026-09-30 and its cron is Sunday 03:00, so the first
window is 2026-10-05. The zero run count is the schedule, not a broken workflow.

GitHub disables scheduled workflows after ~60 days of repository inactivity, and
this repo's schedule has never produced a single run. Land this change together
with a `workflow_dispatch` run so the split is actually exercised before the
next cron.

## Consequence for the rest of the plan

Nothing in the capability-pinning work can be validated by CI until this lands,
and this cannot be validated until defect B lands. Expect to validate sections 1
and 2 of `house-fix.md` locally with `workflow_dispatch` afterwards.

title: IRQ ring is not drained before the first installHandler
description:
Section 1.6 of `~/.opencode/plan/house-fix.md`. A real hole, currently latent.
**Separate issue — do not fold it into the capability-pinning fix.**

## The defect

From boot until the first `installHandler`, **nothing drains the IRQ ring**.
`house_irq_push` (`rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/irq.rs:55`) drops the
record once the 256-entry ring is full. At a 100 Hz timer that is saturated in
under three seconds, so every IRQ between boot and first driver init is lost.

Nothing is currently broken by it — the timer has no `handlerTable` entry — but
it is a real hole and it is why "start the dispatcher at boot" keeps recurring
as an idea.

## Why it matters for the fallback choice

If the `poll`-guard fix for defect A1 does not hold its premise, fallback 6c is
"start the dispatcher at boot rather than lazily inside `installHandler`". That
fallback only actually fixes the ring-drop hole if the dispatcher is started at
boot — so the two are related, which is exactly why this must stay a separate
issue rather than being silently absorbed.

## Scope

Do not design the fix here beyond stating the hole. The fix depends on which
fallback path defect A1 takes.
## Steps to Reproduce

Boot and read `irqDrops` (or the `house_irq_push` drop counter) from `dmesg`
**before** the first `installHandler`, with a 100 Hz timer running and nothing
else consuming IRQs. At 100 Hz the 256-entry ring saturates in under three
seconds, so the counter must be sampled inside that window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The drop is observed and counted before the first `installHandler`
- [ ] A decision is recorded: drain the ring from boot, size it for the window, or document the loss as accepted with the bound stated
- [ ] `make check` green, and the boot-time IRQs before first driver init are accounted for
notes:
## Resolution (2026-11-03)

Decision: **drain the ring from boot**, and make any residual loss counted.

Implemented:
- `H.Interrupts.startDispatcher` (idempotent) is called at the top of
  `house_main`; `installHandler` still starts it for any caller that runs
  first. The dispatcher therefore consumes the SPSC ring from the first
  Haskell instruction.
- `house_irq_push` now counts a full-ring drop in `RING_DROPS` (AtomicU32),
  exported as `house_irq_ring_drops` (HAL, H FFI, `c-abi.md` + baseline). Boot
  reports `[house] irq: pre-dispatch ring drops=N`; `lsdev` adds
  `ring drops=N` (monotonic, next to the existing endpoint `irq drops=`).
- Non-vacuity: Rust unit test `irq::tests::ring_full_counts_drops` fills 256
  entries, proves the 257th increments exactly once, and that draining does
  not. Gate: `scripts/qemu-irq-dispatch.exp` asserts the boot report is zero.

Premise correction: the 100 Hz timer does **not** enter the ring. `c_handle_irq`
handles intid 27 directly (rearm + EL0 preemption) and only the else-branch
calls `house_irq_push`. SGIs 0/1/7 and intids 29/30 are likewise handled
without a push. The ring's producers are SPIs (virtio slots 48..80) and any
other enabled INTID; those are enabled only during driver init, which installs
forwarding in the same init. So the pre-dispatch window has no producer in any
current boot path — 0 drops on all 19 shell boots in a full `make -k check`
run — and the bead's "saturates in under three seconds" bound was wrong.

Bound recorded: after the dispatcher starts it drains every 20 ms (pipe wake or
timer fallback); a producer that fills 256 entries inside one window is now
counted instead of silent. Before the dispatcher starts the only loss possible
is from a producer not yet enabled, and the boot report makes any such loss
visible.

Verified: `make rust-check`, `haskell-check`, `lint`, `house-irq-dispatch-check`,
`house-check`, `house-shell-check`, `house-preempt-check`,
`house-yield-spin-check`, `house-fault-kill-check` (standalone),
`house-tls-el0-check`, `el0tiny-check`, `dynamic-elf-check`.

Not green, both pre-existing at HEAD (filed separately):
- house-6hy: `dynamic-root.sha256` pin drift blocks `dynamic-root-image`.
- house-gq3: `house-ipc-el0-check` TCG second round fails after the denied
  guess (plus the house-fiu.7 prompt race).
close_reason: Drain from boot: dispatcher starts at top of house_main (installHandler keeps idempotent start); full-ring drops counted via house_irq_ring_drops, reported at boot and in lsdev; Rust unit test + irq-dispatch gate assert it. Premise corrected: timer intid 27 never enters the ring, only SPIs do, so the pre-dispatch window has no producer (0 drops on 19 boots). Gates green; make check remains red only on pre-existing house-6hy (dynamic-root pin) and house-gq3 (ipc-el0 TCG).

title: TCG virtio-blk gate livelocks in an EL1 virtual timer storm
description:
Pre-existing and slot-independent: NOT caused by the 32-slot widening.

## Symptom

The tcg leg of `scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp` livelocks after
`PASS: blk read <slot> 0`, before the next command (`write /a hello`) is even
echoed. QEMU sits at 97-99.8% CPU, expect is idle, and no further UART output
ever arrives. It is intermittent: one pristine run got as far as the
hostile-image mount stage before stalling in the burst loop.

## Measured signature

Reproduced with the harness plus `-monitor unix:/tmp/m.sock,server,nowait`
appended to the `--` args:

- `info registers` sampled repeatedly while it spins: the guest cycles
  through `house_uptime_ns_raw`, `house_timerfd_due`, `c_handle_irq` and
  house-libc internals. Under `-d int` the log is ~97k `Taking exception 5
  [IRQ]` lines; the dominant ELRs are inside `c_start_secondary` (the idle
  `wfe`), `is_aligned_to` and `house_sched_yield+0x394`.
- `RING_HEAD == RING_TAIL == 1` (read via the monitor `xp` on the .bss
  addresses from `nm`). Exactly ONE interrupt ever reached
  `house_irq_push`, so the storming interrupt is not a virtio slot SPI — it is
  an SGI or the EL1 virtual timer (INTID 27).
- `waitForCompletion` (`Blk/Server.hs`) is bounded at 200 x
  `threadDelay 2000`, so the blk used-ring poll is not what blocks.

## Proof it predates the 32-slot change

Reproduced identically on a stashed pristine HEAD tree, with the pristine
harness, at slot 7 (device parked there by `-M virt,virtio-mmio-transports=8`):
same stall point (`blk read 0 0 hello-blk`), QEMU at 99.6% CPU.

## Prime suspect

Two agents program the same counter. `threadDelay`/timerfd arms
`CNTV_TVAL_EL0` through `house_timerfd_*`, while `c_handle_irq`'s INTID 27
arm (`c_start.rs`) rearms it unconditionally from
`__c_house_timer_interval`. Each one undoing the other's deadline would give
exactly this: a bounded 400 ms wait that never expires because the timer is
re-armed underneath it.

## Why it matters

`house-virtio-blk-check` is in neither `check` nor `check-tcg`, so CI never
sees it, and the nightly job runs all its gates in one sequence, so a stall
here costs every later gate too. Until this is fixed the blk gate cannot be
moved into `check-tcg`.

## Suggested approach

Debug-loop it: instrument the INTID 27 path with the existing UART trace
points, log `__c_house_timer_interval` and the programmed `CNTV_TVAL_EL0`
across a `blk read`, and confirm which of the two agents keeps re-arming.
Then give one of them ownership. Related: `house-fiu.1` (bound the device poll
+ client `callTimeout`) touches the same timeout path.
notes: 2026-10-05 CI EVIDENCE (important, narrows this): after the 32-slot change landed, nightly run 37236978644 ran `house-virtio-blk-check` on ubuntu-24.04-arm / QEMU 8.2 / TCG and it PASSED - 'PASS: virtio-blk ok' with capacity=131072 sectors, no FAIL lines in the whole run. So the livelock does NOT reproduce on the GitHub runner; it is specific to this macOS host (HVF and TCG both). That makes it a host-timing bug, not a portable one, and means the gate can move into check-tcg anyway. Debug on the macOS host, and treat a green CI run as no evidence either way.
close_reason: Resolved-at-HEAD: 5/5 TCG PASS at ~121s (was 616s every-step-45s) + hvf PASS 132s on stock HEAD, no code change. poll() byte-identical since Nov 2; patch tried and reverted unlanded (no failing behavior remains). Detail in closing comment. Gate TCG-trustworthy; move into check-tcg left as suite-shape follow-up.

comments.author: mimi
comments.text:
RE-SCOPED: this is not a livelock, and it is not macOS-host-specific.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (macOS, QEMU 11.1.2, tree at 97a5ffd)

1. Reproduction rate: 3/3 PASS over the TCG leg
   (`make house-virtio-blk-check TCG_ONLY=1`). The gate does not hang. It
   passes. It is pathologically SLOW: ~13 min per run, against a harness
   budget of 45 s per expect.

2. Where the time goes (timestamps injected into a /tmp copy of
   scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp; scripts/ itself untouched). Every step
   costs ~45-46 s:

      +0s   saw welcome / saw prompt / dmesg framework online / virtio scan slot 0
     +46s   virtio scan device_id=2 at slot 31
     +47s   blk init / blk status
     +48s   blk write 31 0
     +49s   blk read 31 0
     +50s   blk write 31 1
    +187s   blk read 31 1          <- 137 s across 4 commands
    ...     every subsequent step +45/+46 s, uniformly, to the end

3. THE SAME PATH IS NOT SLOW ON CI. Nightly run 37236978644 (the run this
   bead cites as proof the bug is host-only) passes this gate but takes
   10 min 09 s for it, with the identical shape: `blk read 31 0 hello-blk`
   at 21:42:22, `ns ls` at 21:43:54 (92 s), `blk read 31 0 still hello-blk`
   at 21:44:41 (47 s), `blk sync ok` at 21:45:31 (50 s), burst scans at
   21:51:41 (90 s). The earlier note "CI is green, therefore this is
   host-specific" is wrong: CI is green *despite* the same 45 s-per-step
   pathology. QEMU 8.2 TCG on ubuntu-24.04-arm is affected exactly as much
   as QEMU 11.1.2 TCG on this host. The discriminator between the two is
   the accelerator (TCG slow, hvf fast), not the host.

4. Hypothesis 4a (timer frequency) is DISPROVEN. `uptime` (CNTVCT-based)
   advanced 0 -> 10 -> 20 s across a 20 s host sleep: the guest clock
   tracks host wall time exactly. `freq/100` is not too small.

5. It is not general TCG slowness, and it is not the blk path. Measured
   round-trip on real command OUTPUT (never the prompt, which matches a
   stale LineEditor redraw):

       hvf smp=2  uptime 40-159 ms
       hvf smp=1  uptime 7-10 ms
       tcg smp=1  uptime 8-10 ms
       tcg smp=2  virtio scan 74 ms, blk init 14 ms, blk write 15 ms,
                  blk read 8 ms, blk sync 103 ms, blk mount 157 ms

   Back-to-back commands on TCG are 8-157 ms. So the blk path is fine and
   TCG is fine.

6. The cost is paid only AFTER THE GUEST GOES IDLE. Same binary, same
   command: `uptime` costs 8-10 ms when commands are sent back-to-back, and
   exceeds a 300 s expect timeout when sent after a 60 s idle. That is the
   gate's shape exactly - it sleeps 1 s between commands.

7. During an idle window, CPU0 is pinned at 100% in a tight loop. QEMU
   monitor, 25 samples over a slow window:

       18/25  PC=0x4023ef34  house_uptime_ns_raw+0x8
        2/25  PC=0x400821cc  vec_irq+0x9c
        5/25  scattered

   and with LR sampled (15 samples), 12/15 are
   `house_uptime_ns_raw+0x8` with X30 = 0x4023f504, which objdump resolves
   to the return address inside `clock_gettime`. So the hot frame is
   `clock_gettime` -> `house_uptime_ns_raw` -> `__udivti3` (a software
   128-bit divide; aarch64 has no hardware 128-bit divide).

ROOT CAUSE, one sentence

While the shell is idle, an RTS-owned thread busy-polls `clock_gettime`,
which on this target compiles to `__udivti3`, and that spin holds the vCPU
that the shell's capability needs - so every command issued after an idle
gap pays ~45 s under TCG, and the gate's 45 s expect timeout is the only
thing standing between "slow" and "red".

WHAT WAS RULED OUT

- "Two agents arm CNTV_TVAL_EL0" (this bead's prime suspect): still
  disproven. house-libc writes no timer register.
- 4a timer frequency: disproven, measurement above.
- 4b level-vs-edge `house_isr_pending`: not where the time goes. The hot
  frame is `clock_gettime`, not the timerfd readiness path.
- is_aligned_to: not a lead (inlined core::ptr glue), as previously noted.

WHAT WAS TRIED AND REVERTED

Removing the u128 divide from both `house_uptime_ns_raw`
(sys/mod.rs:130-137) and `house_uptime_ns` (sys/time.rs:6-14), replacing
it with `(c/hz)*1e9 + (c%hz)*1e9/hz` (64-bit only; `cntfrq` is
architecturally 32-bit so `c%hz*1e9` cannot overflow u64). Verified the
rebuilt ELF no longer calls `__udivti3` from either function. It did NOT
fix the stall: the spin persists, just with a cheaper body. So the divide
was cost-amplification inside a spin that should not exist, not the cause.
Reverted rather than shipped unverified.

WHY THE HARNESS HIDES THIS

scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp synchronises on `-re ">"`, which matches the
LineEditor redraw emitted *before* a command's output, so expect matches a
stale prompt and the harness runs ~1 command ahead of the guest. Its PASS
markers therefore do not measure per-command latency, and because every
step lands just under 45 s the gate stays green while sitting right on the
timeout edge. That is why this reads as "intermittent livelock": a run
slightly slower than the others trips `timeout` and looks like a hang.
Note `PASS: write /a hello` / `PASS: cat /a -> hello` / `PASS: ns ls after
blk` never appear as their own lines in a passing log - they are glued to
guest output, the same desync seen from the other side.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS (not done here)

- Fix the spin, not the divide: make the blocking primitives actually
  block. `epoll_wait`'s `timeout < 0` branch (sys/mod.rs:514-520) calls
  `house_sched_yield()`, which is a no-op for RTS threads (RUN_HEAD holds
  only house-libc pthreads), so it is a pure busy-spin; the `timeout >= 0`
  branch (sys/mod.rs:524-554) spins on `house_uptime_ns_raw()` the same
  way. The non-thr branch already uses `wfi`. This is the prime suspect
  for the idle spin and needs its own bead with its own gate.
- Separately worth doing, now proven: drop the u128 divide from
  `house_uptime_ns_raw`/`house_uptime_ns`. Cheap, provably equivalent, and
  it removes a software 128-bit divide from the hottest libc entry point.
- Re-synchronise the harness on command OUTPUT rather than `>`, and add a
  total-runtime bound, so this class of failure reads as slow instead of
  intermittent-red. `house-fiu.8` (gate-repeat) is the right home.

house-5wj should stay open and be re-scoped to "guest idle-spin starves
the shell capability under TCG", not "livelock after blk read".

comments.author: mimi
comments.text:
Status update: root cause narrowed to the event-manager poll loop, three blocking fixes landed, gate improved 12:46 -> 10:16. Residual 45s/step pattern persists — NOT closing.

What was proved (QEMU monitor sampling, 3-5 Hz, hundreds of samples across 5+ runs):
- 85-92% of vCPU time in house_uptime_ns_raw+0x8, LR always clock_gettime+0x30. FP-chain walk resolves the caller through the RTS scheduler's StgRun return (schedule+0x42c): a Haskell thread looping on getMonotonicNSec.
- The event manager's poll() instant-returns whenever RUN_HEAD[core] is non-empty (has_runnable fast path). RUN_HEAD[0] holds one permanently-runnable-but-never-scheduled house thread (tid 4, state=RUNNABLE, start=start_thread), so every blocking poll returns 0 immediately and the manager loops at MHz, hammering sched_lock. Under TCG that starves the working core (45s steps); under HVF a free core absorbs it (fast). Matches the hvf/TCG discriminator exactly.
- house_thr_mode is hardwired 1 (never written): epoll_wait's wfi branch was dead code; every caller yield-spun.

Landed (all gates green: fmt, clippy -Dwarnings, abi-symbols 479, rust-test, house-virtio-blk-check hvf+tcg):
- f0e4827: nanosleep blocks RTS threads with wfi until the deadline (was: yield+return 0, i.e. threadDelay never waited); u128 divide -> u64-only in both uptime fns (ELF now has zero udiv refs).
- a707c07: epoll_wait blocks RTS threads on wfe instead of the no-op yield; house threads unchanged. Gate 12:46 -> 10:16 (3 identical runs).

Tried and reverted (documented so nobody repeats them):
- pthread_cond_timedwait RTS path wfi-until-deadline: no effect on the early pattern, plus 976s/475s stalls in later phases (missed-wakeup shape). Reverted.
- poll() yield-then-wfe-block (both finite and infinite): boot hangs at welcome (itimer startup poll(-1) never becomes ready; its wakeup comes via condvar after poll returns). Reverted.
- poll(-1) with 10 ms quantum + sev wakeups on pipe/eventfd writes: worse — SEV storm keeps every wfe awake (10:16 -> 21:34 + blk sync I/O error). SEV reverted; quantum kept briefly then reverted with the rest of poll.

Open follow-ups (poll needs a fix that blocks finite waits but preserves the itimer startup handshake; candidate: block only when timeout > 0):
1. The stuck RUN_HEAD[0] thread (tid 4, start_thread, RUNNABLE, never dequeued despite core-0 scheduling activity) is the lynchpin: it makes has_runnable permanently true. Nobody has identified why dequeue never takes the head, or what that thread is waiting for.
2. house_sched_ipi_handler only sets a flag (no dequeue) and house_sched_maybe_preempt_from_isr is an empty stub, so kicked cores never pick up queued work — likely related to (1).
3. epoll_wait for RTS threads now wfe-blocks; verify no caller depends on instant return (none observed in 3 passing gates).

comments.author: mimi
comments.text:
CLOSE VERDICT: resolved-at-HEAD. No code change landed — the storm is gone on stock HEAD, so there is nothing left to fix. The poll patch below was tried in the worktree and deliberately reverted unlanded.

EVIDENCE (macOS host, QEMU 11.1.2, HEAD c5a285d, image rebuilt from clean HEAD, -smp 2, 4G):
- TCG leg `house-virtio-blk-check`: 5/5 PASS, EXIT=0. Wall times: 121s, 121.02s, 120.92s, 121.06s, 121.04s. Old tree (Nov 2): 616s (10:16) with every step at ~45s. That is a 5x shift, identical across 5 trials — the every-step-45s pattern is falsified, not merely lucky.
- hvf leg: 1/1 PASS, EXIT=0, 132s.
- Per-step shape (timestamped /tmp harness copy, scripts/ untouched; run #2): 25 of 26 instrumented sends 0-1s apart (the 1s is the harness's own `sleep 1`). Residuals: one ~44-45s expect (`cat /a` -> `hello` match, still under the 45s budget, PASS) and one +10s gap spanning the multi-step teardown/reinit/drops-assert phase (its sends are indented, uninstrumented). The single slow cat step does not fit the idle-spin profile (zero idle gap before it; neighbours instant) and smells of the documented harness prompt-desync (matches stale LineEditor redraw, runs ~1 command ahead) — house-fiu.8 territory, not this bead.
- Non-vacuity holds: capacity=131072 asserted, 45 PASS lines, EXIT=0.

WHY NOT THE POLL FIX (revert rationale):
- `poll()` in threads.rs is byte-identical to the Nov-2 tree (zero commits to that file since). The Nov-2 spin characterization (has_runnable permanently true via stuck tid 4 -> poll instant-return -> MHz loop) no longer dominates the gate, whatever its current micro-state.
- Debug-loop rule: no failing behavior remains, so landing a scheduler change would be risk without observable benefit. The Nov-2 reverts prove this code area punishes casual changes (boot hang on poll(-1) block; 976s/475s stalls on timedwait wfi; SEV storm). Reverted, tree clean.
- The reverted patch, preserved here in case the spin ever recurs: in `poll()` (rust/crates/house-libc/src/threads/threads.rs), route only infinite waits through yield+rescan (`if has_runnable && timeout < 0`), letting finite waits block in the existing wfe+deadline loop. Infinite waits keep yield+return for the itimer startup handshake; timeout==0 unchanged.

ATTRIBUTION (honest: not bisected, stated as candidates):
- Plausible contributors since Nov 2: 944df10 (IRQ dispatcher starts at top of house_main — reworks boot thread topology/tids), fault-domain work ed68667/528da55/c2adf1d (driver threading), 0340db4 (IPC grants at spawn). Mechanism-level cause of the speedup was NOT pinned to one commit; a bisect was judged not worth it for a footnote once the gate outcome was 5/5 green.
- The Nov-2 follow-ups were NOT re-verified at HEAD and remain open questions, not blockers: (1) whether a never-scheduled RUNNABLE thread still sits in RUN_HEAD (re-probe: QEMU monitor `xp` on .bss RUN_HEAD/RUN_TAIL from `nm`, as in the original signature); (2) `house_sched_maybe_preempt_from_isr` still an empty stub, `house_sched_ipi_handler` still flag-only.

GOAL STATUS: the bead's goal — gate trustworthy on TCG, movable into check-tcg — is unblocked. Not moving it here (suite-shape decision, out of scope).
Neighbour gates (virtio-transport, driver, irq-dispatch) were NOT re-run: with zero code delta in the tree there is no regression surface from this bead.

# Goal
Create `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: mdBook build + linkcheck on every PR, official-Pages-artifact deploy on push to `main` in `mimi1vx/house` only.

- Official flow: `actions/configure-pages` → `mdbook build` → `actions/upload-pages-artifact` (path `docs/book/book/html`) → `actions/deploy-pages` in a `deploy` job with `environment: github-pages`.
- Permissions: workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`; ONLY the `deploy` job gets `pages: write, id-token: write`.
- Concurrency must serialize deploys: `group: pages-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false` (never cancel a main deploy).
- Pin versions: mdBook 0.5.4 (matches local host), mdbook-linkcheck latest compatible. SHA-pin all `actions/*` (repo convention, see check.yml which uses actions/checkout@v7 etc. — resolve the SHAs with `git ls-remote` at authoring time and record them in a comment).

# Exact work (one file: `.github/workflows/pages.yml`)
```yaml
name: pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: pages-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7  # SHA-pin at authoring time
      - name: Install mdBook
        run: |
          cargo install --locked mdbook --version 0.5.4
          cargo install --locked mdbook-linkcheck
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Build book
        run: mdbook build docs/book
      - name: Linkcheck (book only, no web)
        run: mdbook-linkcheck -c docs/book/book.toml docs/book || mdbook build docs/book  # linkcheck runs as mdBook output; fail the job on broken intra-book links
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@vX  # SHA-pin; only needed for upload, harmless on PR
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'mimi1vx/house'
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@vX  # SHA-pin
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'mimi1vx/house'
        with:
          path: docs/book/book/html
  deploy:
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'mimi1vx/house'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/deploy-pages@vX  # SHA-pin, id: deployment
        id: deployment
```
Adjust the linkcheck step to how mdbook-linkcheck is actually wired (it is an mdBook `output.linkcheck` backend, so `mdbook build` already runs it; the explicit step is a loud second pass — keep whichever fails the job on broken links and delete the other; do not keep two steps doing the same thing silently).

plan: **reuse the existing fd/IPC ring, no new `svc`**.

`fdOpen` (`kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Fd.hs:165-183`) resolves paths only through
`vfsLookup`; **no `/dev/*` node exists anywhere in `kernel/`**. So the
virtio-console endpoint (`NS.nsRegister "virtio-con"`) is unreachable from an EL0
`open`. An EL0 program can write to the console but never read a line from it.

## Work

- [ ] Bind a reserved console path (or pre-seed fd 0/1/2) to the virtio-console
      IPC endpoint inside the existing `Fd` layer — **no new `svc` number, no

title: Slice a TCP transport + EL0 socket API
description:
The track-o-os plan's alternatives and step 3 ("no sockets API yet").

## Why it is open now

The deferral condition is met: *"Full TCP stack now — rejected: DNS + bounds +
caps unblock more with less risk; TCP needs retransmit/congestion + socket state
(**follow-up after step 3 green**)."* All 5 of the track-o-os plan's success criteria
are `[x]`, and the DNS slice this was deferred behind is green.

Both net modules still carry explicit no-TCP markers:

- `kernel/Kernel/Driver/Virtio/Net/Stack.hs:420`
- `kernel/Kernel/Driver/Virtio/Net/Server.hs:479`

And `kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Syscall.hs` numbers `0x00`–`0x14` contain no
socket/accept/connect.

## Needs its own slice breakdown before code

This plan explicitly scoped a full stack **out** (*"least state (no
retransmit/congestion/socket table)"*). So pick one first slice rather than a full
stack — e.g. a `tcp connect/send/recv` shell verb in `Server.hs` reusing the
Track H total-decoder pattern.

## Work, once scoped

- [ ] Reuse `Stack.safeIndex` for the TCP header decoder; hostile-input caps per
      sota-code-security 09.
- [ ] Any EL0 socket syscalls mean new numbers plus
      `rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/svc.rs` park predicates and
      `rust/c-abi.md` rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

`make house-virtio-net-check` green hvf+tcg with the new verb exercised.
design:
# house-dx7.6 first-slice breakdown (scoping only, 2026-11-04)

## Chosen first slice

**S1: EL1-shell `tcp` verb — active open + one-segment send/recv + close.
No new svc numbers; the EL0 socket API is slice 2.**

Concretely, `tcp <ip> <port> [payload]` in the House shell, mirroring the
`udpecho`/`dns` verbs:

- `Stack.hs`: `TcpSegment` type + `decodeTcp`/`encodeTcp` (SYN + data
  segments), total (`Either NetError`), `safeIndex`-only indexing.
- `Server.hs`: `netTcp :: Int -> Ipv4 -> Word16 -> String -> H
  (Either NetError String)` plus a single in-flight record in the style of
  `netDnsSeen`; a proto-6 arm in `handlePacket` beside the proto-1/17 arms
  (proto 6 is dropped at the `_ -> return ()` line today); SYN retry bounded
  like `dnsTries` (3 attempts + backoff, no timer wheel).
- `Shell/Commands.hs`: `tcp` parse arm beside `udpecho`/`dns`; the help text
  (`dns` line, "no TCP") updated.
- `Shell/Loop.hs`: `handleTcp` beside `handleUdpEcho`/`handleDns`.
- `kernel/test/Main.hs`: round-trip + hostile goldens beside
  `propDnsRoundTrip`/the dns asserts; shell-parse golden beside
  `shellParseNet`.
- `scripts/qemu-virtio-net.exp`: a `tcp` stanza against a host TCP peer
  (host socat listener via hostfwd; precedent: the socat bridge in
  `qemu-virtio-con.exp`).

Explicitly OUT of S1 (per the plan): retransmit/congestion/socket table,
listening socket, accept/backlog, TCP option parsing (bytes skipped, never
parsed), EL0 syscalls.

## Why this slice (verified against current code 2026-11-04)

- The bead's suggested verb shape holds: shell-verb plumbing exists
  end-to-end (parse -> dispatch -> `runH Net.*` -> print), and `handlePacket`
  drops proto 6 at exactly one line, so TCP slots in without touching the
  ARP/IPv4/UDP paths.
- Transport-before-syscalls: EL0 socket numbers are untestable without a
  working handshake underneath; S1 gives the gate something to exercise with
  zero Rust/c-abi surface.
- Markers confirmed: `Stack.hs:420`, `Server.hs:479` still carry the no-TCP
  markers; `Syscall.hs` numbers `0x00`–`0x14` are fully allocated with next
  free `0x15` (`0x1D`–`0x1F` are pseudo-reqs FAULT_KILL/PREEMPT/FAULT, so any
  new numbers stay `<=0x1C`).

## Slice 2 cost (EL0 socket API, deferred — not this slice)

New numbers at `0x15+`. Per number, the touch points are:

- `Syscall.hs`: constant + contract doc.
- `svc.rs`: `HOUSE_SVC_*` + `EL0_REQ_*` consts, a `house_*_should_park`
  validate-then-park predicate (trap-side buffer/path bounds, Haskell
  decides), a `c_handle_sync` park-gate arm, and a `house_svc_dispatch`
  match arm (pattern: fd/dir validate-then-park, or BRK/FORK always-park).
- `rust/c-abi.md`: svc dispatch section rows + per-symbol table rows.
- EL0 wrapper (house-el0-tiny / userspace `.s`) + shell binding if exposed.
- No mask widening: `house_svc_mask_*` is u32, `0x15` fits.

## Hostile-input caps (sota-code-security 09)

Wire bytes are attacker-controlled (guest peer via SLIRP); the trust boundary
is `handlePacket` -> `decodeTcp`:

- Length-gate first (mirror `decodeIpv4`/`decodeUdp`): segment <20B -> Left;
  dataOffset outside 5..15 -> Left; hdrLen = dataOffset*4 > len -> Left.
- Options (hdrLen>20) skipped, never parsed in S1 — no option-parse bombs.
- IPv4 totalLen already bounds the TCP payload; the rx frame is already
  capped at 4095B (`Server.hs` rx path).
- Seq/ack/window treated as opaque Word32 — no state machine to poison (no
  retransmit/congestion per the plan).
- SYN retry bounded (3 attempts + backoff like `dnsTries`, no timer wheel);
  single in-flight record reset per verb call (like the `netDnsSeen` reset);
  received payload truncated to the print budget (mirror `take 256`).
- Pure goldens must include: truncations at 0/19/20B, bad dataOffset
  (0, 4, 16), hdrLen>len, trailing-padding tolerance.

## Acceptance gate

`make house-virtio-net-check` green hvf+tcg with the new `tcp` verb
exercised in `qemu-virtio-net.exp`.
close_reason: S1 landed as commit 14c73b4: Stack.hs TcpSegment codec (total, safeIndex-only, hostile caps), Server.hs netTcp active-open + one-segment send/recv + close with x3 SYN retry and single in-flight record + proto-6 arm, shell tcp verb + handleTcp, host goldens (round-trip, 0/19/20B truncations, bad offsets, hdrLen>len, options-skip, trailing tolerance, shell-parse), net harness tcp stanza vs socat echo peer. Gates: make house-virtio-net-check green hvf+tcg (PASS tcp echo hello-tcp both legs), make haskell-check green (fourmolu/hlint/cabal incl 11 new tcp goldens), neighbour make house-shell-check green. No Rust/c-abi surface; no listen/accept, retransmit/congestion, socket table, or option parsing (slice 2+).

title: Step 9: bound the device poll and add a client callTimeout
description:
Step 9, `~/.opencode/plan/house-phase4-loadbearing-shell-and-gates.md`.
**Blocked** on the capability-pinning fix (`house-1hc.1`).

## The problem

`waitForCompletion` is `threadDelay 2000` x 200 = up to 400 ms
(`Blk/Server.hs:105-122`). With step 8 done the service thread now blocks inside
it, so at 400 ms per request a 32-deep queue fills in 12.8 s and every later
caller gets `QueueFull`.

## Why it is blocked

Not started: its measurement (`SPIKE_MEM=4G`, both accelerators) cannot be taken
while `house-virtio-blk-check` hangs on `main`.

## Work

- [ ] **Measure before assuming.** Under TCG the completion path may be slower
      than under HVF. Run `make house-virtio-blk-check` and `make house-fs-check`
      at `SPIKE_MEM=4G` both accelerators first and record the observed
      completion latency. The current 400 ms poll step is **untuned, not
      specified**.
- [ ] Tighten the poll to `threadDelay 200` x 40 — the same 8 ms ceiling, 10x
      better latency. Used-ring completion is IRQ-driven, so the poll interval is
      only a fallback.
      - If 8 ms is too tight under TCG, keep the ceiling at 20 ms (100 x 200 us)
        rather than raising it back to 400 ms.
- [ ] Client side uses `IPC.callTimeout` at a bound above the device ceiling
      (propose 50 ms), so a wedged device yields `WouldBlock` + a dmesg line
      rather than a queue-wide stall. `callTimeout` already logs
      (`Endpoint.hs:290`).

## Acceptance Criteria

`make house-virtio-blk-check` green under hvf **and** tcg with no `WouldBlock`
line in the dmesg the harness asserts on.

## Risk

This step changes device timing on a path three gates depend on. **Do not bundle
step 9 with step 10.**
notes:
## Landed 2026-10-07

Poll bound: `200 us x 100` = a 20 ms ceiling, replacing `200 x 2 ms` = 400 ms.
This bounds the **failure path only** — a completing request returns on the
first poll whose used-ring entry matches, so `blk read` latency is unchanged.
Deliberately *not* a latency fix.

**Measurement** (`clock milliseconds` arm around `blk read` in
`scripts/qemu-virtio-blk.exp`, `SPIKE_MEM=4G`, both accelerators):

- tcg: **10 ms**
- hvf: 28 ms on a single low-load sample; alternating A/B runs of the old
  and new binaries gave old 392/229 ms and new 69/456 ms, i.e. host and
  scheduler noise with no signal about the ceiling.

The 8 ms first choice sits below the measured TCG round-trip, so this bead's
own 20 ms fallback applies: 2x the TCG number. The ceiling never goes back
to 400 ms.

`awaitCompletion` now lives in `Blk/Completion.hs` with the poll action
injected, so the bound is falsifiable off-target. Verified by restoring the
400 ms budget and confirming the new host test fails there.

**The `callTimeout` bullet is DEFERRED to house-fiu.2.** `reqEp` has no
sender today: `blkBlockDev` wires `mapRead`/`mapWrite` straight to
`blkReadBlockBytes`/`blkWriteBlockBytes`, the shell's `blk read`/`blk write`
go direct, and the `QueueFull` branch is reachable only over the endpoint
reply path. The only way to give a client a `callTimeout` is to re-route
`blkBlockDev` through `reqEp` — which is step 10, and this bead forbids
bundling step 9 with step 10. Until then the bead's acceptance clause ("no
`WouldBlock` line in the dmesg the harness asserts on") is vacuous.

**Signature deviation from the plan.** The plan asked for
`awaitCompletion :: H (Either BlkError ()) -> H (Either BlkError ())`, but
that type carries two shapes for the three states the loop distinguishes
(done / still outstanding / device error), so the plan's own two tests
cannot both hold. Landed as
`H (Either BlkError Bool) -> H (Either BlkError ())`: `Right True` done,
`Right False` outstanding, `Left` device error.

`house-5wj` stays open and out of scope. A green run here is explicitly not
evidence about it.

- [x] Order is now: clear IRQ forwarding -> take the endpoint list and thread
      list out under `drvSem` -> release `drvSem` -> `freeEndpoint` each ->
      `killH` each. `freeEndpoint` before `killH` keeps the join bounded,
      because a thread blocked in `recv` on a freed endpoint gets
      `NoSuchEndpoint` (`Endpoint.hs:255-259`) and exits.

      `VTrans.virtioTeardown` cleans up after it. Order: `unregisterDriver` ->
      `virtioTeardown` -> `c_reset_slot`.

      **and** both threads being killed. The `readIrqDrops` half needs a GIC.

- [ ] A `blk init 0` / `blk teardown 0` x 3 cycle in `house-virtio-blk-check`,

title: Step 15: scripts/house.exp prompt helper; convert 124 prompt waits
description:
Step 15, `~/.opencode/plan/house-phase4-loadbearing-shell-and-gates.md`.
Not blocked. This was also decided up front in Phase 4: build a shared Expect
helper library rather than patching harnesses one flake at a time.

## The bug it fixes, stated precisely

383 `expect {` blocks and **124 `-re "> "` prompt waits** across 32 harnesses,
all hand-written, all matching a prompt against a stream the kernel also writes
`dmesg` lines and EL1 kill logs to.

`03b1066` had to *delete* two prompt waits because the kill log garbled `> ` into
`>[kill]`. Deleting the assertion removed the hazard rather than the cause.

## Work

- [ ] New library with `house_prompt {label}`, `house_send {cmd}`,
      `house_expect {re label}`, each doing its own `catch {exec kill -9
      [exp_pid]}` and `eof` handling so no harness repeats that boilerplate.
- [ ] The helper matches the prompt as a **line-anchored** pattern and drains
      interleaved non-prompt output before waiting, so a stray dmesg line cannot
      eat the prompt.
- [ ] Convert in one mechanical commit, one harness per hunk, no behaviour change
      beyond the prompt matching. Do **not** convert harnesses opportunistically
      in the same commit as a behaviour change — that is what made `03b1066` /
      `6e0b314` hard to review.

## Acceptance Criteria

Run the full `nightly.yml` gate list locally before pushing; `make check` green.

## Risk

This touches 32 harnesses in one commit. It is mechanical, but it is 124 call
sites and a typo in the helper fails several gates at once. This is the one step
whose blast radius exceeds its conceptual size.

## Related Tcl trap

In Tcl, `-re {"> "}` searches for the literal `"> "` because braces suppress
substitution, so it matches nothing and every command looks like a hang. And a
corrected `-re "> "` still matches the line editor's prompt redraw during echo,
reporting 0 ms for everything. Match each command's **output** pattern instead —
the echo can never contain it.

title: ipc-el0 gate flakes: second el0pp rendezvous double pp fail (~10%)
description:
house-ipc-el0-check intermittently fails at the SECOND 'ipc el0pp pp' (post-guess): both EL0 sides print 'pp fail', exit 1/1, harness times out waiting for 'served ok'.

Evidence (all at HEAD 528da55 unless noted):
- Full 'make check' red: hvf leg passed, tcg leg failed this way (first pair ok both legs).
- Isolated 'make house-ipc-el0-check': hvf failed the same way.
- Exact-harness tcg loops: 3 fails / ~35 runs (~10%); S1 worktree (ed68667, pre-S2) reproduces identically 1/15 -> pre-existing, NOT an S2 regression.
- Timestamped failing run: first pp fail lands ~0s after the second 'ipc el0pp pp' send (fast errno), second pp fail lands ~40s later (= full 8x5s EAGAIN budget), then ok server=1 client=1. Asymmetric: one peer dies instantly, the other starves waiting for it.
- First rendezvous never failed in ~50 runs; no-guess variant (two back-to-back el0pp) 15/15 pass (weak evidence, p~0.17, guess involvement unproven either way).
- Passing legs show no pin drift; dmesg on passing runs shows only the expected 'ipc deny pid=Pid 5 ep=0' (the guess).

Hypothesis (unconfirmed): grant-after-spawn race in handleIpcEl0pp (kernel/Kernel/Shell/Loop.hs): U.runElf publishes the pid with empty grants and forkHs the EL0 entry BEFORE the shell thread runs U.grantEndpoint. If the EL0 side reaches its RECV/CALL trap first (warm second boot vs shell thread stalled on userSem), hasGrant denies -> instant EPERM pp fail; the surviving peer then burns 40s of EAGAIN and fails honestly. Matches the 0s+40s signature exactly.

Suggested confirmation: catch a failing run with a trailing 'dmesg' and look for 'ipc deny pid=.. ep=<pp-id, nonzero>'; or extend build-probe/ipc_pp.s fail path to print x0 errno.
Suggested fix direction (not bundled): install grants before EL0 start (e.g. spawn takes a grant list, or a start-gate held until grantEndpoint lands). Test-only mitigations (retry the second rendezvous in the harness) would mask a real kernel race; prefer the kernel fix.
close_reason: Root cause: grant-after-spawn race in handleIpcEl0pp. runPreparedBound published each ipc_pp pid with empty grants and forkH'd the EL0 entry before the shell thread's post-hoc grantEndpoint; the new side's first RECV/CALL could beat the grant to userSem, hasGrant denied EPERM (instant pp fail), peer burned 8x5s EAGAIN (~40s). Confirmed by window-widening probe: deterministic 0s+42s double pp fail with 'ipc deny pid=Pid 3 ep=0' (pp endpoint is id 0; no guess in that run). Fixed by threading a grant list through runElfInWithGrants into the publish point before forkH. Verified: gate-repeat house-ipc-el0-check N=10 green (20/20 hvf+tcg), house-ipc-check + house-userspace-check green, haskell-check green. Commit 0340db4.

assertion test.

title: Map virtio MMIO into per-driver page tables so device access runs at EL0
description:
`house-review-and-plan.md` Phase 3 step 41 (`[medium, stretch]`).

## Its precondition is now met

The plan stated: *"only after 37-40 are green and the CI gate has been stable for
a week."* Never scheduled by any later plan — the precondition is now satisfied.

## What

Map each driver's virtio MMIO window into its **own** page tables and give it
its **own ASID**, so a driver fault is contained to its address space.

## Scope

The Rust HAL half only touches device registers, so this is a paging change
rather than a rewrite. It needs a fault boundary that survives an EL0 driver
fault, and real supervision — `forkSupervisedIO` landed in `2bc6ffc`, so that
half is done.

## Acceptance Criteria

Add a fault-injection case to `make house-driver-check`.

## Priority note

This is **stretch**. The plan itself says items 1-4 are the better use of the
same effort.
design:
# house-oz9.11 scoping breakdown (scoping only, 2026-11-04)

## Verdict

Scope recorded, bead stays OPEN. No code in this slice. Three implementation
slices S1–S3 below, or explicit deferral (recommended default per the plan's
own priority caveat — see Cost/risk). The bead's stated acceptance
(fault-injection case in `house-driver-check`) belongs to S3, not here.

## Precondition check (verified live 2026-11-04)

- `forkSupervisedIO` landed: `kernel/H/Concurrency.hs:56-58`
  (`forkSupervisedIO act = IO.forkIO (act \`catch\` handler)`, log-and-end,
  machine keeps running). Callers in all four driver servers —
  `Blk/Server.hs:164`, `Con/Server.hs:508`, `Net/Server.hs:225`,
  `Transport.hs:176` — plus `Init.hs`. Supervision half: done, confirmed.
- Rust HAL register-touch surface (paging change, not rewrite): `mmio.rs`
  `mmio_r32`/`mmio_w32` (single-register `ldr`/`str`, EL1 preconditions),
  `virtio_{blk,con,net}.rs` `slot_base` with `checked_mul`/`checked_add`
  defense-in-depth, `virtio_probe.rs:5` `VIRTIO_BASE 0x0a000000` + slot stride,
  `virtio_transport.rs:116` init/notify/invalidate. All device access funnels
  through these — S1 re-points the mapping, not the accessors.
- No per-driver page tables today: grep for `pdir|page_dir|init_page_dir`
  under `kernel/Kernel/Driver/` returns nothing. Drivers run in EL1 Haskell
  kernel context. S1 is greenfield plumbing, not a migration of existing roots.
- ASID machinery exists for EL0 processes and is reused, not reinvented:
  `userspace.rs:75` `asid_for_pdir` (8-bit, wrap at 250, `ASID_MAP_CAP` 64),
  `userspace.rs:270` `init_page_dir`, `mmu.rs:188` `house_mmu_set_ttbr0`
  (TTBR0 update with TLBI ordering). Reuse for driver roots.
- Fault-containment precedent: `Process.hs` reap-on-fault paths (0x1D
  FAULT_KILL park → process reaped, core keeps running), demand-pager
  `DemandNoMem` reap arm (`Process.hs:2602`).
- Gate harness exists: `Makefile:234` `house-driver-check` (house-build +
  initrd, `scripts/qemu-driver.exp`, hvf+tcg).

## Threat classification (sota-sandboxing BUILD mode)

- Untrusted CODE: an EL0 driver can fault (bad VA, wild MMIO offset) or spin;
  containment must survive it — fault boundary kills only the driver.
- Untrusted INPUT: virtio register bytes are device-influenced (QEMU virtio
  device); lengths from `qsize`/request fields already handled via
  `checked_*` + invalidate-before-read (`rust/c-abi.md` hostile-input notes).
- Boundary choice: MMU hardware boundary — per-driver TTBR0 root + own ASID.
  Above the floor for untrusted in-process code (hardware page tables, not a
  language jail). Layers, each failing closed: (1) allowlist mappings (own
  slot window only, Device attrs, XN, nothing else); (2) EL0 sync-fault →
  kill+reap, never panic/halt; (3) supervised restart via `forkSupervisedIO`;
  (4) existing `checked_*` + `dc ivac`/`cvac` input validation stays in EL1 HAL.
- Residual risks listed per slice below.

## S1: per-driver page-table plumbing + ASID wiring in HAL/userspace

Map each driver's virtio MMIO window into its own TTBR0 root; no EL0 execution
yet (mapping only — access still from EL1, so S1 is testable without the
privilege change).

- `rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/mm/vm.rs` `house_vm_mmap:328-428`:
  MMIO needs Device (nGnRnE) attributes, NOT Normal cacheable — `vm.rs`
  currently maps Normal RAM. Either a mapping-mode flag or a new
  `extern "C"` helper (e.g. `house_vm_map_mmio`) with Device attrs +
  allowlist check (addr within own `VIRTIO_BASE+slot*STRIDE` 0x200 window).
  VA choice (identity vs fixed driver-VA alias) decided in S1; record it.
- `rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/userspace.rs` `asid_for_pdir:75`,
  `init_page_dir:270`: allocate per-driver ASID, install per-driver TTBR0
  root. ASID budget: `ASID_MAP_CAP` 64, wrap at 250 with all-ASID flush —
  S1 counts live driver roots against the cap and verifies the wrap path
  covers driver roots.
- `rust/crates/house-hal-aarch64/src/mmu.rs` `house_mmu_set_ttbr0:188`:
  reuse as-is (TTBR0 + TLBI ordering).
- Haskell side: per-driver `VM.PageMap` (`kernel/H/VirtualMemory.hs:82`
  `setPage`), mapping helper in the `Process.hs:2554` `mapOneSegment` pattern
  (overlap rejection, `checkedAddWord`), driver registry holds
  (slot → pdir/ASID); Haskell FFI decls for any new `extern "C"` symbol in the
  `Transport.hs` `c_*` binding style.
- Residual: wrong Device-vs-Normal attr is silent corruption (stale device
  reads / speculative access) — S1 gate must assert PTE attrs, not just
  presence.
- Gate: `make rust-check` + host mapping-layout test asserting slot window →
  Device PTE (beside `kernel/test/Main.hs` load asserts) +
  `house-userspace-check` green. NOT the fault-injection case (that's S3).

## S2: EL0 fault containment + supervision via forkSupervisedIO

Move driver execution to EL0 under its S1 root so a driver fault is contained
to its address space; the fault boundary survives and the supervisor restarts.

- Reuse `0x1D` FAULT_KILL pseudo-req (`Syscall.hs`; no new svc numbers):
  EL0 sync-fault from a driver TTBR0 context attributes to the driver pid and
  reaps only it. Per-driver roots make this true by construction — a shared
  root would make S2 unsound, hence S1 first. `svc.rs` trap-side
  validate-then-park pattern applies; fault path is trap-side, no new park
  predicates expected.
- Supervision: existing `forkSupervisedIO` endpoint servers
  (`Transport.hs:176`, per-driver `Server.hs` sites) restart the driver
  endpoint; machine keeps running. S2 wires restart to the reaped driver pid.
- IRQ decision (record in S2): keep GIC + `registerIrqForwarding` dispatch in
  EL1, deliver to the EL0 driver via endpoint (already the pattern in
  `Transport.hs` init) — no EL0 GIC mapping. Alternative (map GIC) rejected:
  violates allowlist layer.
- DoS note: a spinning EL0 driver pins its capability; preempt path exists
  (`house-preempt-check`) — S2 sets a preempt/watchdog budget for driver pids.
- Gate: fault-kill gate + `house-fork-check` + `house-driver-check` green
  (restart observed via dmesg/ns, no injection stanza yet).

## S3: fault-injection gate case (the bead's stated acceptance)

- `scripts/qemu-driver.exp`: new stanza driving a bad MMIO offset / unmapped
  VA from the driver context; expect FAULT_KILL + supervised restart +
  `make house-driver-check` green hvf+tcg.
- This and only this slice closes the bead's acceptance criterion.

## Cap/ABI implications (`rust/c-abi.md`)

- No new svc numbers (0x1D FAULT_KILL reused; driver IPC uses existing
  endpoints; `house_svc_mask_*` untouched).
- New `c-abi.md` row(s) conditional: zero if S1 reuses `house_vm_mmap`
  unchanged; one row (userspace.rs/vm section + per-symbol table row) if S1
  adds a `house_vm_map_mmio`-style Device-attr helper. Budget one row; Device
  attrs likely force it.
- TTBR0 window note (`0x01000000–0xFFFFFFFF`, 8-bit ASID, `VMALLE1IS` wrap)
  gains a driver-roots sentence in S1 if the VA/wrap decisions change it.

## Hostile-input / fault-surface notes (per slice)

- S1: window allowlist exactly own slot's 0x200 bytes, Device-nGnRnE, XN,
  never Normal cacheable, never Executable; EL0 never computes MMIO addrs —
  Haskell/EL1 validates slot once, HAL enforces the window. TLB: ASID-tagged
  entries + `VMALLE1IS` on wrap; driver-root teardown must shoot down
  (`VAE1IS`+SGI1 per c-abi note) before freeing pages — else use-after-free
  alias. Driver holds no other slot windows, no RAM beyond its queues, no
  TTBR1.
- S2: out-of-window access → translation fault → kill (fail closed); no path
  from driver fault to core halt (reap, don't panic); IRQ stays EL1-mediated.
- S3: injection stanza is the inside-the-sandbox probe — hostile offsets,
  unmapped VAs, and queuePA tampering each must end in kill+restart, never in
  silent mapping of another window.

## Priority caveat + cost/risk framing (branch decision)

- The plan's own words: stretch; items 1-4 are the better use of the same
  effort. That caveat still holds — nothing in this scoping overturns it.
- Honest cost: S1 touches TTBR0/ASID/shootdown + PTE-attr correctness (silent
  corruption class on error); EL1→EL0 is a privilege change re-auditing every
  FFI register access; three slices each with hvf+tcg gate time. Medium-high
  complexity.
- Payoff is containment that only binds when drivers actually fault; current
  drivers are in-tree Haskell with a low observed fault rate. The boundary pays
  when out-of-tree/untrusted drivers arrive.
- Recommendation: keep this bead OPEN with scope recorded; schedule S1 only
  when (a) items 1-4 are done, or (b) a driver fault escapes to the core —
  then S2 becomes P1. Deferral is the rational default, taken explicitly
  rather than by drift.

Stanza boots a real virtio-blk driver (narrowed+supervised root) and drives offset/unmapped/queuepa through 'driver fault': each parks a genuine 0x1D FAULT_KILL via the real slot protocol (test-only trigger, honestly documented - live EL0 execution stays S2-deferred), the watch attributes pdir-keyed, reaps only that driver, re-arms a fresh root, endpoint/health checks survive. rust-check (2 new host tests, +1 c-abi row justified), haskell-check (probe/refusal/parse goldens), neighbours virtio-blk/transport/fault-kill all green.

title: A store to a plain RO page must yield EFAULT or a kill, never elr+4
description:
Step 18 of `house-phase2-correctness.md`; also review-and-plan step 26 / audit M5.

## The acceptance signal that is still unmet

The plan's wording: *"A store to an RO page delivers `EFAULT` or kills, **never
`elr + 4`**."*

`rust/crates/house-boot/src/c_start.rs:307` still returns `elr.wrapping_add(4)`.

## The path

`c_start.rs:260-308` — for `DFSC 0x0C..0x0F`, `WnR=1`,
`HOUSE_USER_VA_MIN..=HOUSE_USER_VA_MAX`, non-COW page — falls through to
`return elr.wrapping_add(4)`. So the store is **silently discarded and EL0 is
told it succeeded**.

## Why this needs a decision, not just a patch

The code carries a written rationale: read-back is observable, and parking would
livelock the loader's stub probe loop. So the two options are:

- park on a distinguishable request kind, or
- add the `vm-check` mprotect-RO read-back assertion the plan asked for

No later plan revisits it.

## Acceptance Criteria

`make vm-check` asserts a store to an RO page yields `EFAULT` or a kill, never
silent success.

Note `vm-check` is an expensive memory/MMU matrix and **not** part of the
ordinary per-change gate.
## Steps to Reproduce

1. `mmap` a page in EL0, write to it.
2. `mprotect` it read-only.
3. Store to it again.

Observed today: the store is silently discarded and EL0 continues — the
`c_start.rs:307` fall-through returns `elr.wrapping_add(4)`. The plan's
acceptance signal is that this must deliver `EFAULT` or kill instead.

title: Distill what a real Haskell EL0 binary needs, past the Userspace.Asm gap

`userspace/hs/Userspace/Asm.hs:89-133` — the `Instr` ADT, 50 constructors — has

The GHC-compiled-EL0 route was **abandoned** per the GHC size/Libc spike

title: Enforce parent-child ownership in waitPid
description:
`house-review-and-plan.md` §1.4: *"Parent-child ownership is unenforced —
`waitPid` reaps any non-self process."*

## Why it is open

Still open and only documented. `README.md:35` states it as a known limitation.

## The defect

`kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Process.hs:1153-1180` — `waitPid` looks the pid up in
`procExitMap` with **no parent check**. So any process can reap any other.

## Work

`Process` (`kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Types.hs:53-59`) does not carry a
`procParent`, so:

- [ ] add the field
- [ ] populate it in `forkProc` (`Process.hs:748`) and the EL0 fork path
      (`:897-904`)
- [ ] inherit it across exec
- [ ] check it in `waitPid`

## Acceptance Criteria

`make house-proc-check` and `make house-fork-check` green.

## Scope note

This is a microkernel-correctness item, not a hardening one. Whether an
enforced parent check is the right call for a unikernel with no privilege
boundary is a design decision worth writing down alongside the code.
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fork process A from the kernel shell.
2. Fork process B from process A.
3. Have **A** call `waitPid` on **B**'s pid.
