title: Retune the nine loader/linker caps as one reviewed decision
description:
## Epic context

The dynamic-linking umbrella's own status header names the open branch:
*"B (provenance (ii), GHC's libraries rebuilt against `house-libc`) is unstarted
with the cap retune it needs recorded as its own decision."*

This retune is the prerequisite for that whole branch, so it comes first.

## Why it is one issue and not nine

M1-M3.5, the loader-forgiveness slice (C1-C6, `d77be5a`), the phnum/segment
split with the `ByteString` representation, and **C8 (ABS64 + `DT_VERSYM`,
`011b538`) have all landed.**

Verbatim from the umbrella plan: *"Rows 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 15, 16, 17, and 18 remain a* cap
retune, and that retune is still unauthorised: B1 fixed the representation so the
numbers would mean something … but no cap value moved."*

So the work is one reviewed bound review, not nine independent edits.

## The nine bounds

`kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Loader.hs:54-110`:

- `maxElfBytes` 1 MiB
- `maxSegMemSz` 256 KiB per `PT_LOAD`
- `maxTotalPages` 64
- `maxRelaCount` 4096
- `maxDynSymbols` 4096

`kernel/Kernel/Userspace/Linker.hs:50-57`:

- `maxDependencies` 8
- `maxObjectPages` 64
- `maxTotalPages` 256
- `maxNeeded` (at cap)

## Work

- [ ] Review all nine as one decision and record it in
      `docs/dynamic-linking.md` — the umbrella header says the retune
      "needs recorded as its own decision".
- [ ] `loadElf` is already `ByteString`, so a 16 MiB image no longer forces a
      representation change.
- [ ] Mirror every moved bound in `build-probe/repack.py` (the `MAX_PHNUM` /
      `MAX_SEGMENTS` precedent).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each retuned bound ships a hostile vector that still fails *at* it, in
  `kernel/test/Main.hs`.
- `make check` + `make dynamic-elf-check` green.
- `scripts/dynamic-elf-check.sh` moves from
  `NoSpace: total pages >64 or memsz >256K` on `libm.so.6` to the next named
  bound.

## What

`exec`. This is the only item the future-work proposal still advertised

Row 20 of the M4 gate table: **25.5 MiB resident per mapping process** for the
measured GHC closure.

The M3.1 shared finalized DSO pages already made cross-pid physical sharing

Every dynamic slice so far has deliberately left `kernel/H/VirtualMemory.hs` and

dynamic symbols, 165,975 relocations. It needs the cap retune before it can be
planned at all."*

must move it to SysV hash and unversioned.

## Acceptance Criteria

*cap."*

and the file count asserted by `scripts/qemu-initramfs.exp` must not move.

## S4: ~91-symbol gap closure, sequenced vs the syscall layer + cap revisit

- Gap input (already measured, `docs/dynamic-linking.md` q0g.4 section):
  ~30 libm transcendentals (`acos`…`tanh`, `exp`, `log`, `pow`,
  `ldexp`), POSIX process/file/event (`fork`, `pipe`, `dup2`, `waitpid`,
  `epoll_create`/`ctl`/`wait`, `eventfd`, `sigaddset`/`emptyset`/
  `procmask`, `poll`, `flock`, `fcntl[64]`), termios
  (`tcgetattr`/`setattr`, `isatty`), `sysconf`/`utime`,
  `iconv_open`/`close`/`iconv`, allocation (`malloc`/`calloc`/
  `realloc`/`free`), plus data objects `stderr`/`environ`. ~5x base's
  19-sym gap (base: 16 libm + `clock_gettime`/`clock_getres`/
  `getrusage`/`times`, docs q0g.3 section). ~11 already house-libc
  exports — verify live in-slice against the el0tiny-check allowlist
  and `libc-house.so.0` dynsyms, do not copy the triage's "about 11".

  syscalls (`fork`, `epoll`, `eventfd`, `sig*`, `poll`, …) draw from the

  `Syscall.hs` + `svc.rs` + `rust/c-abi.md` rows (house-dx7.6 S1/S2
  precedent). Stub-vs-real is a per-symbol decision (`compat.rs`
  failing-closed stubs are the precedent: `dlopen`→NULL); data symbols
  (`stderr`/`environ`) need a definition home, not stubs. The final link
  goes `--no-undefined` either way (`mk-house-image.sh:205,261` carry
  it already).
- Cap revisit (house-q0g.1): rows 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 17, 18 for internal

  `maxElfBytes` 16MiB refuses the 20.4MB file; Loader `maxTotalPages`

  decision (q0g.1 precedent: hostile vectors + headroom rationale), not

- Acceptance gate: `--no-undefined` link succeeds; the loader places

- Cost/risk: largest slice. libm wants real implementations

## S2 outcome (executed live 2026-11-04, NOT scope text)

Header decision (open decision, resolved): COMPILE -fPIC AGAINST CONTAINER
HEADERS. No new freestanding headers (neither in-tree nor on-volume), no
-ffreestanding, zero house-provided declarations. Rationale, all verified
live: the 14 C files' system-header closure is fully covered by the
container toolchain (Debian multiarch /usr/include + aarch64-linux-gnu,
gmp.h multiarch, iconv.h/langinfo.h/poll.h in libc6-dev); house-libc
already exports the glibc-spelled U the packages need (__errno_location,
__xpg_strerror_r, nl_langinfo, iconv_open/close/iconv, sysconf, poll --
all present in the 285-export inventory, compat.rs/sys). -ffreestanding
was TRIED and REJECTED on measurement: it disables the hosted
printf->puts fold, so debug.dyn_o emits U=printf instead of U=puts
(U-diff +printf/-puts vs S1 baseline) -- pure U churn for zero gate
benefit. Plain -fPIC reproduces the S1 baseline bit-for-bit at the
T/U-set level (below), so the provenance commitment stays exactly the
S1-measured U set: nothing novel, nothing to re-declare.

triage names iconv/SetEnv/gmp_wrappers confirmed, full list closed):

title: house-ipc-el0-check hvf: first-pairing pp fail, served-ok timeout (follow-up to house-gq3)
description:

## Symptom

```
ns reg pp → registered pp
run /bin/ipc_el0pp pp
pp fail
pp fail
ipc el0pp ok server=1 client=1
FAIL: served ok timeout (RECV/REPLY ring wedged?)
```

Both peers exit 1 on the first round; the harness never sees `served ok`. No denied guess precedes it (guess step never reached), so the EPERM path is uninvolved.

## Reproduced

- `make house-ipc-el0-check`: 1/1 green (hvf+tcg, 2/2 legs) at ~06:30, working tree = HEAD 28beb66 + uncommitted cargo-fmt reflow (if/else one-liners, semantics-preserving; NOT committed, see task-1 report).

Rate so far: ~2 hvf-leg `pp fail` events in ~9 hvf boots (prior run #2 + this gate run 7).

- a9c8a46 (pager: fault-driven demand paging) touched IPC-recv ensure + demand-paging serve timing; EL0 server/client now fault pages on first touch while rendezvousing. An 8-attempt EAGAIN retry (3cfce9b) covers scheduling lag but not a page-fault park arriving mid-RECV/CALL.
- Alternatively the 5s pairing bound is still marginal under hvf SMP variance and both sides give up simultaneously (same signature as the TCG root cause, different accelerator).

- Capture UART/ring trace on a failing hvf boot (RECV errno sequence per attempt, fault-park interleaving).
- Check whether the failing boot correlates with demand-page serve events for ipc_el0pp pages.
- Do NOT bundle a feature fix here; if the pairing bound is the cause, retune as a trivial pin only.

title: Lower workspace MSRV from 1.100.0 to 1.99.0 — blocks every stable toolchain
description:
Step 1 of `~/.opencode/plan/rust-stable-transition.md`. **[trivial]** This is the
actual bug fix and the unblocker; everything else is bookkeeping.

## The defect

`rust/Cargo.toml` line 9 declares `rust-version = "1.100.0"`, which is above the
latest stable (1.99.0). Cargo therefore hard-refuses to build the workspace on
*any* stable toolchain today.

Reproduced:

```
$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable cargo check
error: rustc 1.99.0 is not supported by the following package:
  p@0.1.0 requires rustc 1.100.0
```

The MSRV was set in `2a38214` ("chore(toolchain): pin rust-version 1.100.0
across workspace", 2026-09-06) while nightly was the only channel that could
satisfy it. It has been a forward-looking declaration ever since, and it is the
thing blocking stable.

Still true in the tree: `rust/Cargo.toml:9` reads `rust-version = "1.100.0"`.

## Fix

`rust-version = "1.100.0"` -> `"1.99.0"`.

All five crates inherit it via `rust-version.workspace = true`, so **no per-crate
edits**.

## Acceptance Criteria

`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable cargo metadata --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml` no
longer errors on MSRV.

## Empirically verified

With MSRV lowered to 1.99.0, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` **compiles
clean on stable 1.99.0**. The only diagnostics are pre-existing `suspicious
definition of the runtime read/write/strlen symbol` warnings, which are
**identical on nightly** — confirmed by running the same clippy invocation on
nightly-2026-09-30. They are host-triple-only (hosted `cargo test` interposes std
symbols) and do not appear on the real gate, which is
`--target aarch64-unknown-none`. **Not a stable-transition regression; do not
"fix" it as part of this change.**

## Nothing else needs nightly

- Zero `#![feature(...)]` attributes in `rust/`.
- The only arch intrinsics in use are `core::arch::asm!` (stable since 1.59).
- No `global_asm!`, no `#[naked]`.
- `aarch64-unknown-none` std ships on stable (tier-2, present in the stable
  manifest's 116 `rust-std` targets). Only the *host* stable toolchain here
  lacks it installed — a local-install artifact, not a channel limitation.
- Everything is zero-dependency (`cargo deny` clean by construction), so no
  third-party MSRV bumps are implied.
## Steps to Reproduce

Verified still true in the current tree:

```
$ grep -n rust-version rust/Cargo.toml
9:rust-version = "1.100.0"
```

Against a scratch copy (project untouched):

```
$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable cargo clippy --workspace --target aarch64-apple-darwin -- -D warnings
error: rustc 1.99.0 is not supported by the following packages:
```

Upstream stable is 1.99.0 (2026-09-28, `b940084d7`). No 1.100/1.101 stable
channel exists.

title: dynamic-root.img pin does not match what mk-dynamic-root.py builds
description:
Pre-existing: NOT caused by the 32-slot virtio change.

## Symptom

`make dynamic-root-image` (and therefore `make check`, which runs it as a leg)
fails at the pin check:

```
sha256sum -c scripts/dynamic-root.sha256
sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match
build/dynamic-root.img: FAILED
```

`scripts/dynamic-root.sha256` pins
`c6d2664ef0043eaa1261fcfb31c232ababc30ab3817b3051808c1edeb07fdb92`
but the build produces
`d52974ede39fddd7a0fe1d34a1a82d91a481c351207e8276f67d002c1a41a590`.

## Proof it predates the virtio change

Reproduced on a stashed pristine HEAD tree with the identical digest
(`d52974e...`), and `house-el0-tiny`, whose
`build/dynamic-probe/root/libc-missing.so.0` is the image's only input, has
no dependency on anything the virtio work touches.

## Two possibilities, not yet separated

1. **Genuine drift.** Something in the `house-el0-tiny` link output changed
   (toolchain, flags, or a genuine source change) and the pin was never
   regenerated. Then `scripts/dynamic-root.sha256` needs re-pinning — but
   re-pinning a hash you have not explained is how a real regression gets
   laundered, so find out which first.
2. **Non-determinism in `scripts/mk-dynamic-root.py`.** If the image embeds
   anything varying per run, the pin can never hold and every host fails
   differently. Cheap discriminator: build the image twice on a clean tree and
   compare the two digests. Equal => case 1; unequal => case 2.

## Also worth checking

`make check` has never run to completion — this leg has been the blocker, so
every leg after `house-dynamic-root-check` in that target is unproven locally.

## Related

`house-fiu` lists "`make house-dynamic-root-check` green locally" as an
unchecked phase criterion; this is the concrete reason it is not.
close_reason: Stale pin attributed and re-pinned: scripts/dynamic-root.sha256 embeds the UNREPACKED EL0 DSO, so any house-el0-tiny edit (here 5c24dda's lint-attribute reason= strings; earlier 453cd4c's toolchain bump) moves it, while the three repacked-artifact pins stay correct. .text/.dynsym/relocs/stripped bytes identical across the change, so the drift was codegen-neutral. make check now exits 0 for the first time.

Attribution, measured. Neither possibility in the issue body is the whole answer, and only one pin is stale.

## Not non-determinism (case 2 is dead)

Two consecutive `make dynamic-root-image` runs produce byte-identical images
(`cmp` clean, both `d52974ede39fddd7a0fe1d34a1a82d91a481c351207e8276f67d002c1a41a590`).
Case 1, genuine drift.

## Only ONE of the four pins is stale

`make initrd` is green: all three manifest checks pass unchanged
(`static-userspace` 20/20, `dynamic-userspace` 7/7, `lib-version` 1/1). Pins
1-3 were not touched by this fix and must not be. `build/initramfs.cpio` was
deleted first so the run could not be masked by mtime.

So the failing pin is `house-dynamic-root-check` (leg 14), not `initrd` (leg 8) —
the issue body's implicit ordering was the one thing it got right, but the cause
is narrower than "the EL0 artifact chain".

## Why one file moves and three do not

The pins split into two families by what they hash:

- `static-userspace`, `dynamic-userspace`, `lib-version` hash **repacked**
  artifacts. `build-probe/repack.py` emits a minimal ELF with no debug sections,
  so DWARF churn never reaches them.
- `dynamic-root.sha256` hashes `build/dynamic-root.img`, which
  `scripts/mk-dynamic-root.py` fills with the **unrepacked**
  `build/dynamic-probe/root/libc-missing.so.0` — `.debug_*` sections included.

Hence any edit to `rust/crates/house-el0-tiny/src/lib.rs`, down to a doc comment,
moves `dynamic-root.sha256` and nothing else.

## Attribution: `5c24dda`, and it is behaviour-neutral

`5c24dda` added `reason = "..."` to two crate-level `#![allow(...)]` attributes.
Built in throwaway worktrees at `453cd4c` and at `5c24dda^` (= `8af1116`): both
produce image `461108f764cd4119314a115133e782e3d9acc59e04c75f2b9e1c5e8f50aa3204`.
HEAD produces `d52974ed…`. The image moved at `5c24dda`.

The laundering test — is anything loadable different? For
`build/dynamic-probe/root/libc-missing.so.0` at `453cd4c` vs HEAD:

    objcopy --strip-debug   5e687f97…  ==  5e687f97…
    .text                    698f75ed…  ==  698f75ed…
    readelf --dyn-syms       e7369053…  ==  e7369053…
    readelf -r               15864317…  ==  15864317…

Identical. Only DWARF moved, so re-pinning records a documented, codegen-neutral
edit rather than hiding a behavioural change.

## Two contributing commits, not one

The pin was already stale before `5c24dda`: `453cd4c` bumped the toolchain
(`rustc 6bb1652a…` → `5c543b0b…`, new `rust/toolchain.lock`, Containerfile, and
the `mk-dynamic-probe.sh` assertions) and re-pinned `dynamic-userspace` and
`lib-version` — both DSO-derived — but not `dynamic-root.sha256`, which is also
DSO-derived. That miss shipped the image as `461108f7…` against a pin of
`c6d2664e…`.

## A measurement trap worth writing down

`mk-dynamic-probe.sh` prints the digest of the **pre-repack** DSO
(`0220a269… libc-house.so.0`), while the pin file hashes the **post-repack**
staged copy (`28aeaa1c…`). Those numbers differ by design. Reading the probe
output as a pin comparison is what makes all four pins look stale.

## Verification

- two consecutive image builds byte-identical
- `make initrd` green, 20/20 + 7/7 + 1/1, pins 1-3 untouched
- `make dynamic-root-image` green (`sha256sum -c` OK)
- `make house-initrd-check` green on hvf **and** tcg
- `make house-dynamic-root-check` green on hvf **and** tcg
- `scripts/qemu-initramfs.exp` still asserts 32 files; staged count still 32

Fix is one line in `scripts/dynamic-root.sha256`: `c6d2664e…` → `d52974ed…`.

title: house-virtio-blk-check is red 5/5 at the house-1hc.1 defect: blk init forks the same capability-pinning dispatcher
description:
Found while landing house-1hc.2. That bead assumed `house-virtio-blk-check`
passes on the buggy tree; measured, it does not.

## Measured on 2026-10-03, commit 44537d6 (tree unchanged by house-1hc.2)

- `make house-virtio-blk-check` (hvf leg) — 4/4 red, `FAIL: blk init timeout`
- `make house-virtio-blk-check TCG_ONLY=1` (the leg `nightly.yml:51` runs) —
  red, `FAIL: blk init timeout`

`house-virtio-blk.exp` is byte-identical to HEAD and the diff touches nothing
on that path, so this redness is pre-existing, not a regression.

## Why the existing gate is wrong about itself

The `INFO` arms in that harness only cover a *missing device*:

```
-re "BlkBadSlot|BlkNotBlk|BadSlot|BadVersion" { puts "\nINFO: ..." }
```

A *hang* never produces those strings — it runs into the hard `timeout` arm at
line 60 and fails. So the "the INFO arms make every assertion optional, hence
it is 8/8 green" reasoning does not hold for this defect: the only way that
gate passes with a blk device attached is if `blk init 7` answers.

## Same defect, one layer up

`Blk.blkServerInit` (kernel/Kernel/Driver/Virtio/Blk/Server.hs:151) calls
`VTrans.virtioInit slot` when the slot is not already initialized. That is the
`Transport.virtioInit` which forks the transport IRQ dispatcher at
Transport.hs:176 — the dispatcher whose `house_pipe_wait` spin in `wfe` inside
unsafe FFI pins the RTS capability (house-1hc.1). `blk init` then forks a
second one for the request endpoint (Server.hs:165).

So `blk init 7` wedges for exactly the reason `virtio init 7` does.

## Why this needs its own bead rather than just a note on house-1hc.1

Two things house-1hc.1's fix should be checked against, and neither is
recorded anywhere today:

1. **house-1hc.1 turning green must turn this green too.** When A1 lands,
   `make house-virtio-blk-check` is the second, independent witness that the
   capability is no longer pinned — it exercises the blk request dispatcher
   (`blkRequestHandler`), which the new irq-dispatch gate never reaches.
2. **Until then the nightly is red.** `nightly.yml:51` runs this target, so
   the nightly has been reporting this failure as long as the defect has been
   present. If the nightly is currently green, that is itself worth asking
   about — the failure mode here is a hang, and a job killed by workflow
   timeout can look like an infra flake rather than a real red.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- After house-1hc.1 lands: `make house-virtio-blk-check` exits 0 on both legs.
- The nightly's `house-virtio-blk-check TCG_ONLY=1` leg reports red for the
  current tree, not green — confirmed rather than assumed.

Do **not** fix this by loosening `qemu-virtio-blk.exp`: making its `blk init`
arm optional again would hide the very failure this bead documents. The
overlapping work on the harness's vacuous-`INFO` design is house-1hc.5.

Fixed a harness race at qemu-virtio-blk.exp:161-168 where drops=([0-9]+) could match a buffer ending at 0 before newline arrived; now single capture requiring terminator. No product change; A1 witness holds.

title: house-posix-check races /sbin/init sh ENOENT output against first shell prompt
description:
## Symptom

`make check` (hvf+tcg, macOS host) at 6d6b68e failed at the hvf half of `house-posix-check`:

```
initramfs: 34 files
init pid 1
init up
> sh: ENOENT
init done
init exit 1
FAIL: saw prompt timeout
make[1]: *** [house-posix-check] Error 1
```

Full log: /private/var/folders/w9/shn0shjj527fkyfbbbgkfng40000gn/T/opencode/house-check-6d6b68e.log (lines 868-945, failing leg at 936-944).
Isolated retry `make house-posix-check` immediately after: EXIT 0, both hvf+tcg halves green.
Retry log: /private/var/folders/w9/shn0shjj527fkyfbbbgkfng40000gn/T/opencode/house-posix-retry.log (hvf PASS lines 64-176, tcg PASS lines 202+).

Passing retry shows the benign ordering for the same bytes:

```
init up
sh: ENOENT
init done
PASS: saw prompt
init exit 1
```

i.e. init's `/bin/sh` child output (`sh: ENOENT`, exit 1 — expected, no /dev/console) lands on its own lines and the `house_prompt ">  "` match (scripts/house.exp) succeeds. In the failing run the same output landed mid-prompt as `> sh: ENOENT` (one space, not the two-space `>  ` signature), so the prompt wait timed out.

## Why not caused by 6d6b68e

HEAD is provenance-only for the init binary: `userspace/init.s` at HEAD~1 is already v3 fork/exec /bin/sh, `house-gen init` diffs clean, and `initramfs-staging/sbin/init` hash is unchanged (`ed170af`). Same race exists before/after; the EDSL change altered no boot bytes.

## Triage (gate flake policy, product-vs-test)

- Shell prompt (`> ` + cursor cell ` \x1b[K\x08`) and init child `WRITE("sh: ENOENT")` share one UART with no newline discipline (documented in scripts/house.exp). Failing run shows byte-level interleave *inside* the prompt signature, not just drained pre-prompt output.
- Leaning product (kernel UART atomicity: concurrent shell-prompt vs init-child writes from different threads/caps can split the `>  ` bytes), but harness ordering also contributes (posix waits for prompt while init is still live; shell-check usually wins the race because it consumes the prompt first).
- Per policy unsure counts as reported, not as flake. No harness change made here; no prompt wait deleted. Second stabilization against this gate must be a kernel bug report, not a harness tweak.

## Repro

1. `make house-posix-check` repeatedly at 6d6b68e (hvf half is the sensitive one).
2. Expect intermittent `FAIL: saw prompt timeout` with the `> sh: ENOENT` garble in the UART log.

## Suggested next step

Serialize prompt vs concurrent init/dmesg bytes (atomic prompt write or hold init-child output until first prompt), or make posix harness deterministically drain `init done`/`init exit 1` before the first `house_prompt` without deleting the wait. Owner to pick product vs test after one more observation; do not close as "flake".
close_reason: Fixed product-side (option A) in 11103a6. Root cause: two unsynchronized PL011 writers split each other's bytes at per-char UART-lock granularity on SMP: the console-consumer thread emitted the shell prompt as separate uart_putc calls (putString prompt + cursor cell + ClearEOL + BS-back) while the svc trap path emitted EL0 WRITE fd 1 per-byte (sh ENOENT, 11 uart_putc holds). An init-child write landing between the prompt's 2nd and 3rd byte produced the observed '> sh: ENOENT' garble, breaking house_prompt's two-space match. Fix: prompt+cursor cell now one PutStr uart_puts unit (kernel/Kernel/Types/Console.hs, Console.hs putStr, Driver/PL011.hs dispatch, LineEditor.getLine); EL0 WRITE holds UART_LOCK across the whole message via crate-internal uart_lock/unlock/putc_locked (uart.rs, svc.rs, no C ABI delta, abi-symbols still 481). Each writer's bytes are now contiguous so the signature cannot split. Verified: make haskell-check green, make rust-check exit 0, gate-repeat TARGET=house-posix-check N=10 passed 10/10 (hvf+tcg, 20 boots), neighbours house-shell-check, house-pid1-check, house-proc-check, house-userspace-check green. No push per protocol.
